subject: 1:00 AM
fact: By 1:00 AM, Sylvira claims to have been alone and feverish in her chambers, with no one else seen. This is the endpoint of her alibi and the earliest possible time the heart removal could have occurred if not performed earlier.
source_quote: Between 12:30 and 1 in the morning, feverish, alone. After that, no one.

subject: 11:30 PM
fact: The end-of-year meeting occurred at 11:30 PM, ending in an argument with Janussi over a private matter.
source_quote: The end-of-year meeting had been at 11:30 PM...

subject: 11:45 PM
fact: At 11:45 PM, Alkrist and A'lai met to discuss how to deal with Janussi, planning the poisoning using midnight tears. This was the operational planning phase of the murder.
source_quote: Eleven forty-five. A'lai and Alkrist, discussing what needed to be done about their mutual problem.

subject: 12:30 AM
fact: Sylvira returned to her chambers around 12:30 AM and remained there, feverish and alone, until at least 1:00 AM, according to her recollection.
source_quote: I returned to my chambers around 12:30... between 12:30 and 1 in the morning, feverish, alone.

subject: 12:30 AM
fact: Sylvira returned to her chambers at approximately 12:30 AM, claiming to have been with her son in the Abyss. This marks the start of her alibi period, which she claims lasted until 1:00 AM.
source_quote: She'd returned to her chambers around 12:30, she thought.

subject: alibi time
fact: She returned to her chambers around 12:30, and saw no one after that.
source_quote: She'd returned to her chambers around 12:30, she thought. After 12:30, she came to her room and saw no one.

subject: budget day
fact: Budget day was the day Janussi initiated his purge, firing Alkrist, canceling Bookwyrm’s research, and destroying A'lai’s work—triggering the chain of events that led to his death.

subject: day of the murder
fact: The murder occurred on a single, well-documented day, with precise witness timings (1 AM, 2–3 AM, 2:30 PM) allowing for a clean, if complex, timeline — though magical interference complicates its interpretation.
source_quote: A'lai had shown up at the Oak Tree Apothecary at half past two on the day of the murder.

subject: Deadwinter evening
fact: Kalan Strongbranch approached Sylvira before Deadwinter evening to plead for his job. This event occurred prior to the murder and established a prior grievance.
source_quote: Kalan Strongbranch had come to her before Deadwinter evening, asking her to intercede with Janussi on his behalf...

subject: Deadwinter evening
fact: Kalan approached Sylvira on Deadwinter evening to request intercession with Janussi; she promised to help but never followed through.
source_quote: Kalan Strongbranch had come to her before Deadwinter evening...

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session, from 12:30 to 1:00 AM.
source_quote: Between 12:30 and 1 in the morning

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: A polymorph spell lasts an hour

subject: Eleven forty-five
fact: The conversation between A'lai and Alkrist about their mutual problem occurred at eleven forty-five, marking the beginning of the recorded timeline of the conspiracy’s aftermath.
source_quote: Eleven forty-five. A'lai and Alkrist, discussing what needed to be done about their mutual problem.

subject: last conversation with Janussi
fact: Sylvira’s final words to Janussi were hostile and unresolved — occurring just hours before his death — making her the last known person to speak with him, and the event a critical timestamp in the timeline.
source_quote: Those were my last words with him.

subject: meeting time
fact: The baths meeting occurred at 11:45 PM between A'lai and Alkrist.
source_quote: Eleven forty-five. A'lai and Alkrist, discussing what needed to be done about their mutual problem.

subject: midnight of Janussi's death
fact: Janussi died at midnight, following a day of delivering verdicts that turned his own authority into a weapon, and the events of that day culminated in a silent, shared decision among multiple parties to end his life.
source_quote: By midnight he was dead.

subject: recent return from Underdark
fact: Sylvira's recent return from the Underdark is the most truthful statement made in the conversation and serves as a pivot point for her willingness to explain her vulnerabilities.
source_quote: I'd recently come up from the Underdark

subject: review day
fact: Review day was the day Janussi’s actions were formally evaluated, and his decisions were ratified—making his murder appear as the inevitable result of institutional dysfunction.

subject: Session Date
fact: The events described occurred during a single, dense session — likely the same day as Janussi’s exposure and dismantling. No calendar date is given, but the temporal compression — from confession to blackmail proposal — suggests a single, high-stakes narrative arc.
source_quote: We had dismantled in a single afternoon.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occurred during an afternoon session of investigation, marked by the contributions of Grygum, Elian, Zalthir, Fembris, and the speaker — a day defined by the emergence of contradictions and the refusal of truth to be easily captured.
source_quote: It was his contribution to the afternoon and I wasn't going to complicate that.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 11:30 PM of Deadwinter evening, the end-of-year meeting.
source_quote: The end-of-year meeting had been at 11:30 PM

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the day careers were made or broken.
source_quote: Budget day. Review day. The day careers were made or broken.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the day of the murder at half past two, with events unfolding through the night and into the next day.
source_quote: A'lai had shown up at the Oak Tree Apothecary at half past two on the day of the murder

subject: the day careers were made or broken
fact: The day Janussi died was not just a day of death, but a day of institutional recalibration—where one man’s ambition destroyed others, and others’ silence destroyed him.

subject: the feast
fact: The feast occurred shortly before Janussi’s murder and was the last public gathering where Alkrist and Kalan were both present; the burning event took place there, marking the point where academic rivalry turned lethal.
source_quote: He apparently burnt something at the feast.

subject: Tomorrow
fact: Fembris Lancer promised to deliver a draft by tomorrow, marking a concrete temporal anchor for the next administrative step in the documentation process.
source_quote: He promised a draft by tomorrow.

subject: alibi verification
fact: Her claim of being with her son after 12:30 is verifiable as an alibi, since she saw no one after returning to her chambers.
source_quote: After 12:30, she came to her room and saw no one.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist washed his hands in a basin of water after burning the vial's label, fearing contamination.
source_quote: he had washed his hands in it, just in case there was any midnight tears on them.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist's hand drifted toward the shelf when asked how he proposed dealing with Janussi.
source_quote: His hand moved toward the shelf before his mouth had finished the sentence.

subject: Alkrist interview preparation
fact: The Alkrist interview is pending, to be bound by Kalan’s truth spell and informed by the feast burning detail.
source_quote: we needed Kalan. And Kalan, apparently, had gone somewhere.

subject: Alkrist’s interrogation under truth spell
fact: Alkrist confessed under Kalan’s truth spell to poisoning Janussi, detailing the use of midnight tears, the re-wrapping of the book, the destruction of the vial label, and the hand-washing in a basin to remove traces. He denied knowledge of the heart removal.
source_quote: The vial's label torn off and tied to the back of the Dead Winter tree as decoration. He was burning the label when Irony and Orrin Glass arrived... I washed my hands in it, just in case...

subject: apothecary intrusion
fact: At half past two on the day of the murder, A'lai arrived at the Oak Tree Apothecary requesting fennel, creating a distraction while a dragonborn entered and collected poison — a separate act from the later theft of the heart and looting of the safe.
source_quote: Alkrist was a dragonborn. Zalthir had caught that this referred to the apothecary intrusion, not whoever had later removed the heart and looted the safe: two separate acts, two separate threads.

subject: blackmail as a career
fact: Blackmail as a career is a known pattern in murder mysteries, and A'lai's actions reflect this — he constructs history as administrative efficiency to mask criminal intent.
source_quote: you often find somebody who treats blackmail as a kind of career... the man who treats blackmail as a kind of career knows how to make his own history sound administrative.

subject: blackmail negotiation
fact: Blackmail may be a way to get information that's very hard to come by.
source_quote: Blackmail may be a way to get it.

subject: Bookwyrm's confrontation
fact: Bookwyrm argued with Alkrist after learning of the poisoning, stormed off, and later acted to conceal the crime by removing Janussi's heart.
source_quote: She had been appalled... and then she was gone... That was Bookwyrm.

subject: Bookwyrm’s confrontation with Alkrist
fact: Bookwyrm confronted Alkrist after learning of the poisoning, argued loudly, stormed off, and was last seen alone with Janussi’s body. Her subsequent actions — including the heart removal — remain unconfirmed but are strongly implied.
source_quote: She went somewhere. He went home. Someone had known about the chalice... That someone was not Alkrist.

subject: budget day at Candlekeep
fact: Budget day at Candlekeep was the day Janussi was killed, used as cover for a targeted elimination under the guise of fiscal restraint.
source_quote: Budget day. Review day. The day careers were made or broken.

subject: Candlekeep monograph exchange
fact: Two individuals in one afternoon sought to associate with Thorin for academic gain, revealing institutional norms around prestige.
source_quote: Two men after a monograph in one afternoon.

subject: Colloquium
fact: The colloquium was an exceptionally well-received event that prompted multiple participants to offer superlatives, theories, and written contributions — though the substance of the event was obscured by the focus on interpersonal dynamics and hidden logistics.
source_quote: The talk had gone well. Extraordinarily popular, as I was informed by several people on my way out.

subject: conspiracy dismantled in a single afternoon
fact: The conspiracy that ended Janussi's life was dismantled in a single afternoon by the group, exposing A'lai and the hidden motives behind the murder.
source_quote: a conspiracy that had ended a man's life and that we had dismantled in a single afternoon

subject: conspiracy exposure
fact: The conspiracy behind Janussi’s death was exposed in a single afternoon through testimony, recovered evidence, and the zone of truth, revealing that Alkrist acted as the instrument, A'lai as the architect, and others as silent accomplices.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz heard the observation that what's going on with him is what's important, and filed it without comment.
source_quote: I heard it said aloud and filed it without comment.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed that the narrative of workforce restructuring matches the story A'lai would have constructed for himself.
source_quote: This is, I noticed, exactly the narrative A'lai would have constructed for himself, and had probably already constructed, somewhere in the months between deciding Janussi needed to die and watching us pull the whole account apart in an afternoon.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized A'lai's need for discretion as an accurate observation that needed no elaboration.
source_quote: I heard it and recognized it for what it was: an accurate observation that needed no elaboration.

subject: Daz interviews Sylvira
fact: Daz conducted a deliberate, empathetic interview with Sylvira, uncovering her framing and motive tied to Menzoberranzan prejudice.
source_quote: I believe I said you were framed... She took it. It was accurate, if not warm.

subject: end-of-year meeting
fact: The end-of-year meeting at 11:30 PM focused on planning a new library dedicated to the Great Wheel of Planes, a joint vision between Sylvira and Janussi, and ended in a private argument.
source_quote: It ended in an argument about a personal, private matter, she said.

subject: feast
fact: The feast was a drab, unchanged affair; Sylvira left early as the flu began, and no one observed her near the kitchen or consuming honey.
source_quote: The same drab affair it always was, right down to the dishes... I'd left early when the flu began coming on.

subject: feast burning
fact: Alkrist burned something at the feast, a detail unflagged until Grygum recalled it.
source_quote: there's something in the list about what Alkrist burned at the feast — you should ask about that.

subject: feast burning
fact: At the feast, Alkrist burned an object — likely symbolic or ritualistic — that may represent the destruction of Kalan’s rejected proposal or an act of ideological purging; this act remains unexplained and is now a key line of inquiry.
source_quote: He apparently burnt something at the feast — that's what it says.

subject: feast burning
fact: Something was burned at the feast by Alkrist. The detail was recorded in an unflagged list and later recalled by Grygum as potentially relevant to the investigation.
source_quote: He apparently burnt something at the feast," came the confirmation. "That's what it says.

subject: Fembris hunts Kalan
fact: Fembris set out to hunt Kalan Strongbranch, the First Reader, to bind the Alkrist interview.
source_quote: I'm gonna have to hunt Kalan down... Let me go, let me go.

subject: framing incident
fact: Someone has used Sylvira's likeness to commit acts she could not have performed, framing her for a 'horrible tragedy' that remains unspecified but appears to involve sabotage or murder.
source_quote: your likeness has been seen moving around, doing things you couldn't possibly have done?

subject: framing of Sylvira
fact: Sylvira was framed for Janussi’s murder using magical impersonation; evidence of her likeness was placed at the scene, suggesting knowledge of her routines and appearance — likely by someone with access to her quarters or personal effects.
source_quote: Your likeness has been seen moving around, doing things you couldn't possibly have done.

subject: gelatinous cube capability
fact: Glabbagool can eat through walls and safes, but chooses restraint to maintain stealth in investigations.
source_quote: I guess I could have eaten through the safe. It would have taken a while. Walls don't stop us. I can eat through walls.

subject: gift wrapping
fact: The gift wrap for the deadly book had a clean, deliberate cut, separate from incidental tears, indicating premeditated preparation.
source_quote: A clean cut, straight as a rule, separate from all the ragged tears.

subject: gift-wrapping deception
fact: The book used to deliver midnight tears was wrapped in paper that was later cut and re-wrapped — evidence of deliberate misdirection. The clean cut on the wrapping paper, revealed by a restoration cantrip, indicates the gift was prepared to deceive Janussi into believing it was a genuine present.
source_quote: A clean cut, straight as a rule, separate from all the ragged tears. Someone had taken something sharp to this paper...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum claims he made up the principle 'Once you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however unlikely, must be the truth,' though he knows he didn't.
source_quote: I made it up myself

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum concluded the clean cut indicated the wrapping paper had been deliberately cut and reused, suggesting premeditation.
source_quote: That is not a crime of opportunity. That is a crime of preparation.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized the wrapping paper had been used to wrap a deadly book.
source_quote: The gift wrap for the deadly book.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum retrieved a crumpled piece of wrapping paper from the dining hall trash and noticed a straight edge where there shouldn't be one.
source_quote: I turned it over in my hands. Torn in several places, the way paper tears when you're unwrapping something with reasonable enthusiasm. But there was something else. A straight edge where there shouldn't be one.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum used a cantrip to restore the wrapping paper to its original state and observed a clean cut, separate from the ragged tears.
source_quote: The paper did the rest. There it was. A clean cut, straight as a rule, separate from all the ragged tears.

subject: Grygum’s discovery of Janussi’s note
fact: Grygum discovered Janussi’s note, which revealed that Janussi had not only rejected Kalan’s methodology but had characterized it as a vanity project.
source_quote: Janussi hadn't just rejected the proposal. He'd characterized Kalan's entire framework as a vanity project... as though the investigation of crime were an indulgence, a hobby, a *conceit* Kalan was pursuing for his own entertainment.

subject: Grygum's revelation of the principle
fact: Grygum claims authorship of the principle 'Once you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however unlikely, must be the truth' — though it is not his original — and this act of intellectual ownership becomes a symbolic anchor for the team’s methodology.
source_quote: I made it up myself.

subject: Grygum uncovers Janussi's note
fact: Grygum discovered and analyzed Janussi’s damning academic note rejecting Kalan’s methodology.
source_quote: I read it... Oh boy, this starts out with some real academic insult.

subject: hand-washing
fact: Alkrist washed his hands in a basin of water after burning the vial's label, attempting to remove traces of midnight tears.
source_quote: He had washed his hands in it, just in case there was any midnight tears on them.

subject: heart removal
fact: After Janussi’s death by poison, his heart was ripped from his chest — an act not committed by Alkrist, who was unaware of it. Sylvira and Alkrist both imply Bookwyrm, who was alone with the body after their argument, performed this act.
source_quote: Ripped out his heart? What? His heart was ripped out? ... That was Bookwyrm.

subject: Janussi's assassination
fact: Janussi was murdered after a single day of deliberate provocations—firing staff, canceling research, and destroying archives—that turned multiple individuals against him, culminating in a coordinated killing that was disguised as an administrative tragedy.

subject: Janussi’s death
fact: Janussi’s death was not an impulsive act but the culmination of a carefully constructed conspiracy, later dismantled by the party in a single afternoon. The event has been retrospectively framed by A'lai — and potentially by Candlekeep’s administration — as workforce restructuring, RIFs, or budgetary pressure, masking assassination as organizational efficiency.
source_quote: The man who treats blackmail as a kind of career knows how to make his own history sound administrative.

subject: Janussi's final day
fact: On Janussi's final day, he delivered three separate verdicts — one to Alkrist (dismissal of research), one to Bookwyrm (succession denial), and one to A'lai (performance review) — each independently motivating them to act against him, without coordination.
source_quote: Budget day. Review day. The day careers were made or broken.

subject: Kalan’s proposal rejection
fact: Kalan’s Threefold Proof methodology was formally blocked by Janussi, derailing his career and possibly motivating his actions.
source_quote: All of it. Dismissed as solipsism. Shelved.

subject: last argument with Janussi
fact: Sylvira’s final argument with Janussi was over a personal, private matter — not a character insult — and she maintains he was justified in dismissing Kalan.
source_quote: It ended in an argument about a personal, private matter... He was right to want him gone.

subject: mind control claim
fact: Alkrist falsely claimed he was under mind control to invalidate his compelled testimony, revealing desperation and guilt.
source_quote: I am under mind control, and everything I have said is so true.

subject: monograph authorship
fact: A monograph cannot have multiple authors; a duograph or acknowledged contribution is acceptable.
source_quote: It's a work that has one author

subject: motive
fact: Teles Ahvoste's motive was jealousy — passed over for Keeper of Tomes despite being older and more skilled than Janussi, a grudge sustained for nearly twenty years.
source_quote: Teles had remained hostile toward Janussi for nearly twenty years, passed over for Keeper of Tomes despite being older than Janussi and generally considered the more skilled practitioner.

subject: poisoned book delivery
fact: The delivery and opening of the poisoned book was a carefully orchestrated act of assassination. The perpetrator planned for Janussi’s death and the subsequent disposal of evidence, indicating deep forethought and emotional detachment.
source_quote: That is not a crime of opportunity. That is a crime of preparation. They had planned for what happened after the gift was opened, which means they had planned for what happened after Janussi was dead.

subject: poisoned book wrapping paper trail
fact: The wrapping paper from the poisoned book was taken to a third-story apartment in Janussi's chambers, which remains unvisited and contains unresolved evidence about Kalan that does not require an interview to yield.
source_quote: We knew the wrapping paper from the poisoned book had been taken there, and we hadn't gone back.

subject: poisoning and body alteration
fact: Janussi was first poisoned via a book by Alkrist, then his body was altered — likely via polymorph — to appear as if his heart had been ripped out, with the vial label tied to the Dead Winter tree and midnight tears used to obscure evidence.
source_quote: The vial's label torn off and tied to the back of the Dead Winter tree as decoration.

subject: poisoning of Janussi
fact: Janussi was poisoned with midnight tears, applied to a gift-wrapped book — 1001 Tashalian Nights — by Alkrist. The poison was carefully concealed, and the wrapping was later discarded in the dining hall trash, bearing a clean cut suggesting premeditated tampering.
source_quote: Someone had taken something sharp to this paper, and then wrapped it back around the contents, and tied the bow... That is not a crime of opportunity. That is a crime of preparation.

subject: poisoning of Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is suffering from a slow-acting poison that mimics winter flu symptoms; it was administered to incapacitate her and prevent her from testifying, indicating the perpetrator feared her knowledge or potential cooperation.
source_quote: She kept shuddering anyway... a cold she clearly felt in her bones.

subject: polymorph contradiction
fact: A two-hour gap in sightings contradicts the one-hour duration of a standard polymorph spell, implying a more complex magical mechanism.
source_quote: She'd been seen coming down the stairs between two and three. That's a minimum two-hour gap. A polymorph spell lasts an hour.

subject: polymorph suspicion
fact: It is suspected that Bookwyrm used a powerful polymorph spell to transform Janussi's heart after removing it, concealing the true cause of death.
source_quote: Does he think Bookwyrm knows a powerful polymorph spell?

subject: proposal rejection
fact: Janussi formally rejected Kalan Strongbranch's Threefold Proof methodology, labeling it solipsism. This rejection was documented in writing and later discovered as evidence in Janussi's chambers.
source_quote: Janussi had reviewed Kalan Strongbranch's proposal for new criminal investigation methodologies, found it to be solipsism, and had blocked it.

subject: proposal rejection
fact: Janussi formally rejected Kalan Strongbranch’s Threefold Proof methodology, labeling it solipsism and a vanity project — a dismissal that effectively buried Kalan’s professional credibility and may have motivated his involvement in Janussi’s murder.
source_quote: Janussi had reviewed Kalan Strongbranch's proposal... found it to be solipsism, and had blocked it.

subject: reused wrapping paper
fact: The gift wrap was possibly reused, but the clean cut suggests it was cut from a larger sheet and deliberately resealed to conceal the book's contents.
source_quote: Could be someone who reuses wrapping paper... but there was something else. A straight edge where there shouldn't be one.

subject: safe unopened
fact: Alkrist's safe remains unopened despite multiple opportunities for access, with Glabbagool revealing — after the fact — that he could have consumed it, but the team chose stealth over brute force.
source_quote: I guess I could have eaten through the safe. It would have taken a while.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira stopped mid-thought and doubled back to ask if anyone had seen her after the party.
source_quote: Then she stopped mid-thought and doubled back to the question I'd asked a minute earlier. "Did you ask me if anyone saw me, after?"

subject: Sylvira's alibi
fact: Sylvira’s alibi — being with her infected son in her chambers after 12:30 AM — is verifiable through her physical condition and the plague’s effects, and is contradicted only by dubious eyewitnesses.
source_quote: I had no wristwatch... no reason to track the precise hour... after that, no one.

subject: Sylvira’s alibi timeline
fact: Sylvira claims to have been with her son in the Abyss from shortly before 12:30 AM until returning to her chambers around 12:30, then alone and feverish until 1:00 AM. No one else is confirmed to have seen her after that hour, making her a credible witness against false sightings.
source_quote: She'd returned to her chambers around 12:30, she thought. ... Between 12:30 and 1 in the morning, feverish, alone. After that, no one.

subject: Sylvira's confession
fact: Sylvira admitted to her final words with Janussi and suspected Kazryn Nyantani of the murder.
source_quote: Those were my last words with him... That bitter old hag... who always resented Janussi for ditching her in favor of me.

subject: Sylvira's emotional breakdown
fact: Sylvira broke down while discussing Kazryn Nyantani, admitting personal guilt and referencing a 'frumpy old boar' — an unexplained metaphor tied to academic rivalry and emotional trauma.
source_quote: This was my fault.

subject: Sylvira’s final words with Janussi
fact: Sylvira’s final words with Janussi were spoken during an argument, moments before his death.
source_quote: Those were my last words with him.

subject: terrain as truth
fact: In the Underdark, terrain is the only reliable evidence; magic and testimony are shifting surfaces over fixed facts.
source_quote: In the Underdark, the one thing that didn't lie was terrain.

subject: the alpha's throat sound
fact: An alpha stationed at the door made a pointed sound in its throat, signaling Fembris Lancer’s departure after his failed inquiry about the missing investigators.
source_quote: An alpha stationed there made a pointed sound in its throat. Fembris collected himself.

subject: the cheese memory
fact: Glabbagool’s memory of cheese is a real, persistent emotional anchor, and his expression of grief over its absence is treated as authentic by Grygum.
source_quote: I remember when there was cheese. Perhaps if we had some cheese.

subject: the colloquium
fact: The colloquium was a gathering where multiple participants presented theories, debated methodology, and sought monographs, leading to the recognition that magic does not make evidence meaningful but adversarial.
source_quote: The talk had gone well. Extraordinarily popular, as I was informed by several people on my way out. ... Elian said the paper had a whole section on it: the myth of the person. ... Magic was just another moving surface. The facts underneath it were still fixed.

subject: the counterfactual thesis
fact: Elian proposed a counterfactual thesis: that even an unsolved murder could yield value if documented as a methodological case study, and Grygum acknowledged its academic merit.
source_quote: Elian said even if we failed to solve the murder, even if all I could write was that these techniques would have helped, the academic community would still approve.

subject: the feast burning
fact: Alkrist burnt something at the feast — an act referenced in the investigation notes as potentially binding evidence.
source_quote: He apparently burnt something at the feast," came the confirmation. "That's what it says.

subject: the interview with Sylvira
fact: Daz interviewed Sylvira, who admitted to being framed and named Kazryn Nyantani as a suspect, while revealing her infernal heritage and the prejudice she faced.
source_quote: She started thinking aloud about suspects... 'This was my fault.'... 'Being the convenient target isn't exclusive to any one city.'

subject: the investigation timeline
fact: The investigation timeline was clean because every piece fit a little too well: A'lai’s visit, the dragonborn’s arrival, the collection of poison, and the separation of the heart theft from the apothecary intrusion.
source_quote: The party walked me through it. The timeline was clean in the way timelines are when every piece fits a little too well. A'lai had shown up... a dragonborn had arrived... The poison was collected. A mess was made. Alkrist was a dragonborn. Zalthir had caught that this referred to the apothecary intrusion, not whoever had later removed the heart and looted the safe: two separate acts, two separate threads.

subject: the monograph correction
fact: Grygum corrected Elian’s use of 'monograph' to mean a single-author work, and later claimed to have invented the phrase 'Once you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however unlikely, must be the truth,' though he had heard it before.
source_quote: I'm sorry — it would not be a monograph if we wrote it together. ... 'Once you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however unlikely, must be the truth?' ... 'Yes,' Grygum said, with tremendous dignity. 'I made it up myself.'

subject: the monograph correction
fact: Grygum corrected the misuse of 'monograph' to mean a single-author work, and asserted that co-authorship invalidates the term, establishing scholarly norms.
source_quote: I'm sorry — it would not be a monograph if we wrote it together.

subject: the monograph exchange
fact: Fembris Lancer and Elian both sought monographs with Grygum or Thorin, revealing a cultural practice in Candlekeep where authorship equals prestige.
source_quote: First Fembris, now Elian. Two men after a monograph in one afternoon. That told me something about how this library keeps score.

subject: the monograph pursuit
fact: Two men, Fembris Lancer and Elian, separately approached Grygum and Thorin seeking to co-author monographs, revealing a cultural currency of academic credit in Candlekeep.
source_quote: First Fembris, now Elian. Two men after a monograph in one afternoon. That told me something about how this library keeps score. ... Elian said it'd be great if we could write a monograph together.

subject: the myth of the person
fact: The myth of the person is the false assumption that the dead shed their performances and tell only the truth, when in fact they still forget, misattribute, and believe convenient lies.
source_quote: The myth of the person. The assumption that death is a transparency, that the dead have shed their performances and will now simply tell you what's true. They don't. They're still themselves. They forget, misattribute, have things they'd rather believe about what happened.

subject: the safe being eaten
fact: Glabbagool offered to eat through Alkrist's safe, noting walls do not stop him, and Zalthir acknowledged that while destruction was possible, stealth was the goal.
source_quote: I guess I could have eaten through the safe. It would have taken a while. ... Walls don't stop us. I can eat through walls. ... If the goal was to be destructive, I could've just punched the safe. But we were trying to be sneaky.

subject: the safe's potential breach
fact: Glabbagool’s offer to eat through Alkrist's safe was accepted as a valid, previously unconsidered investigative option, and added to the open threads.
source_quote: I guess I could have eaten through the safe. It would have taken a while. ... I added the safe to the list.

subject: the safe's unopened status
fact: Alkrist's safe remained unopened throughout the investigation, and its continued closure was noted as an open thread in the document.
source_quote: At the end of this document it says, open threads: Alkrist's safe, unopened.

subject: the Sylvira contradiction
fact: The Sylvira lookalike was seen in two locations separated by a two-hour gap, which exceeds the duration of a polymorph spell, indicating a more complex magical or non-magical explanation.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is an institution where administrative cruelty masquerades as efficiency; its internal RIFs, budget cuts, and research purges created the conditions for Janussi’s murder, and its leadership may be complicit in covering up systemic corruption.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is an institution where powerful spells like polymorph are accessible to any individual with sufficient standing, suggesting that Bookwyrm did not need unique access to perform the body alteration — anyone could have done it.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep operates as an academic ecosystem where scholarly credit is currency, monographs are status symbols, and intellectual contributions are measured by attribution rather than truth, creating a culture that incentivizes collaboration for prestige over clarity for discovery.
source_quote: Two men after a monograph in one afternoon. That told me something about how this library keeps score.

subject: Candlekeep Keepers
fact: The Candlekeep Keepers are scholars entrusted with safeguarding knowledge. Janussi’s murder represents a violation of their sanctum and a failure of their protective protocols, suggesting an external threat with intimate knowledge of their culture.
source_quote: a scholar who'd spent a lifetime reading things carefully, never noticed.

subject: Daz

subject: Dragonborn

subject: Great Readers

source_quote: Great Readers included. She named Teles Ahvoste directly.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a city where accumulating too many enemies leads to inevitable resolution by the city itself — a system the city got right. It operates through lethal efficiency, and its influence may extend into the conspiracy surrounding Janussi’s death. A'lai’s background suggests alignment with its culture of calculated survival.
source_quote: In Menzoberranzan, you do not get to accumulate that many enemies before the city resolves the problem for you, which is one of the less subtle things the city got right.

subject: Menzoberranzan

source_quote: if that was a trick the drow use in Menzoberranzan — to twist the knife in their unsuspecting victims — it was a poor one.

subject: Menzoberranzan

subject: Menzoberranzan

subject: A'lai
fact: A'lai is a drow with Underdark connections, possibly Menzoberranzan connections, currently holding a conspiracy that ended a man's life and was dismantled in a single afternoon, and he pays in knowledge, not gold or books.
source_quote: A'lai, moreover, is a drow. He might have information that Daz needs.

subject: A'lai
fact: A'lai is a drow with Underdark connections, possibly Menzoberranzan, who is now compromised by the exposed conspiracy.
source_quote: A'lai. A drow with Underdark connections, possibly Menzoberranzan connections, currently holding a conspiracy that had ended a man's life and that we had dismantled in a single afternoon.

subject: A'lai
fact: A'lai is not merely a suspect—he is a broker of secrets, a drow with access to Menzoberranzan’s hidden networks, and the only person who can provide the truth about the patron paying for his survival; his silence is the only asset worth acquiring.

subject: A'lai
fact: A'lai is the most reliably underpriced resource in the world because he knows what others have done and has chosen not to use it — that is the only price I am interested in collecting.
source_quote: What he knows about whoever is paying Menzoberranzan rates to keep a nobody drow evoker alive and functional: that is the only price I am interested in collecting.

subject: A'lai
fact: A'lai treats blackmail as a kind of career and knows how to make his own history sound administrative.
source_quote: The man who treats blackmail as a kind of career knows how to make his own history sound administrative.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist believed Bookwyrm had reacted with appallment to his plan and had stormed off after their argument.
source_quote: Appalled, he said. She had been appalled, and they argued, and then she was gone.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist believed he had a fantastic, superb relationship with Janussi.
source_quote: I had a fantastic, superb relationship with the man.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist claimed he was under mind control and therefore forced to tell the truth against his will.
source_quote: He was being forced, he said, to tell things that were true, against his will.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist confessed he had placed midnight tears on the book, unwrapped it, coated it, and re-wrapped it.
source_quote: The Oak Tree Apothecary, the stolen vial, peppermint spilled on the counter floor. Daral's present, unwrapped and coated in midnight tears and carefully re-wrapped.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist entered Janussi's chambers with a rehearsed performance of grief, intending it to be witnessed.
source_quote: The performance started before he sat down. ... he deployed grief the same way: deliberately, as an announcement he wanted witnessed.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist gave the accounting of the conspiracy: A'lai set it in motion, and he carried it out, and he was the hand that executed the plan.
source_quote: Alkrist had given us the accounting of it: A'lai as the one who set it in motion, himself as the hand that carried it out.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist had been studying the Midnight Tears method from 1001 Tashalian Nights and had bookmarked the relevant section.
source_quote: The book was on a shelf, bookmarked. ... There was a class ... about what you find in someone's room telling you more than what they'd ever say with their face. I found the book anyway.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist insisted he did not kill Janussi, only poisoned the book.
source_quote: I didn't actually kill him. I just put some poison on a book.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist is a bronze-scaled individual who publicly expressed grief over Janussi’s death, but his rehearsed demeanor and access to Janussi’s chambers suggest possible involvement. He is unaware that a truth spell is active, and his statements are being scrutinized for hidden intent.
source_quote: He entered Janussi's chambers with the careful energy of a man who had rehearsed his arrival, and then deployed grief the same way: deliberately, as an announcement he wanted witnessed.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist is a dragonborn whose identity was confused with the intruder at the apothecary, though Zalthir later distinguished the intrusion from the later heart theft and safe looting.
source_quote: Alkrist was a dragonborn. Zalthir had caught that this referred to the apothecary intrusion, not whoever had later removed the heart and looted the safe: two separate acts, two separate threads.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist is a dragonborn; implicated in the apothecary intrusion, not the later removal of the heart or looting of the safe.
source_quote: Alkrist was a dragonborn.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist is a person of interest linked to the feast, where something was reportedly burned. The detail was noted in a list but initially unflagged until Grygum recalled it, prompting further inquiry.
source_quote: When you talk to Alkrist, there's something in the list about what Alkrist burned at the feast — you should ask about that.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist is dragonborn and had burnt something at the feast.
source_quote: When you talk to Alkrist, there's something in the list about what Alkrist burned at the feast — you should ask about that.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist is dragonborn and was present at the feast where something was burned — an act not yet explained, but potentially tied to the blocking of Kalan Strongbranch's proposal and the subsequent murder of Janussi.
source_quote: When you talk to Alkrist, there's something in the list about what Alkrist burned at the feast — you should ask about that.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist is referenced by Zalthir as the one who planned the poisoning of Janussi using midnight tears, but did not kill him.
source_quote: I didn't actually kill him. I just put some poison on a book

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist is the individual who administered poison to Janussi via a book, acted under perceived mind control during interrogation, and confessed to involvement in the plot while insisting he did not kill Janussi directly.
source_quote: I just put some poison on a book.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist poisoned Janussi using midnight tears from the 1001 Tashalian Nights, re-wrapping the book after coating it. He admits to the act but denies killing Janussi, claiming the heart removal was done by someone else — likely Bookwyrm.
source_quote: I didn't actually kill him. I just put some poison on a book.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist resented Janussi for dismissing his germ warfare research as dangerous and telling him he showed no leadership potential.
source_quote: dismissed, told his germ warfare research was dangerous and should be stopped, told he showed no leadership potential.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist was genuinely confused when told Janussi's heart had been ripped out.
source_quote: Ripped out his heart? What? His heart was ripped out?

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist was one of Janussi’s subordinates, fired and humiliated on budget day; he later became the hand that carried out Janussi’s murder, acting in coordination with others, and now holds knowledge of the conspiracy that could be leveraged for blackmail.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist was pleased when Thorin took his grief at face value, mistaking sincerity for sincerity.
source_quote: He took it as sincere. He was pleased.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is referenced by Sylvira as the one who pushed hardest against Kalan's investigative controls.
source_quote: Bookwyrm who had pushed hardest against it

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm opposed Kalan’s proposal for investigative controls over Janussi’s work, calling it absurd. She later argued with Alkrist after learning of the poisoning, stormed off, and was alone with Janussi’s body afterward — potentially responsible for the heart removal.
source_quote: When Janussi had raised it at some point, it was Bookwyrm who'd felt it was absurd. Bookwyrm who had pushed hardest against it.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm opposed Kalan’s proposed investigative controls and restrictions, calling them absurd, and may have obstructed early detection of the murder.
source_quote: When Janussi had raised it... Bookwyrm who'd felt it was absurd. Bookwyrm who had pushed hardest against it.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm was a senior librarian at Candlekeep whose research was destroyed by Janussi; he was among those who desired Janussi’s death and may hold ancillary knowledge of the institution’s internal power struggles.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm was appalled by Janussi's death, argued with Alkrist, stormed off, and is suspected of having accessed a powerful polymorph spell to alter Janussi's body after death, though she claims no responsibility for the heart-ripping.
source_quote: That was Bookwyrm," I said, mostly to myself.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is a man who, after reclaiming the poisoned book, delivered the poison to himself with the same care he used to deliver it to others, indicating self-sacrifice or self-punishment.
source_quote: In the process of reclaiming it, he had licked his finger, licked the book, then licked his finger again.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is operating on an instinct he can't articulate: that the one with the Lesser Restoration isn't ready to spend it, and arguing won't make healing come sooner. He consumed the poison himself while reclaiming it, with the same care he used to deliver it to others.
source_quote: He had licked his finger, licked the book, then licked his finger again.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is operating on an instinct that the one with Lesser Restoration isn't ready to spend it, and arguing won't make healing come sooner.
source_quote: Daral was operating on an instinct he couldn't quite articulate: that the one with the Lesser Restoration wasn't ready to spend it, and that arguing wouldn't make the healing come any sooner

subject: Daral
fact: Daral reclaimed the poisoned book and licked his finger twice after licking the book, demonstrating the same care in delivering poison to himself as he had in delivering it to others.
source_quote: Daral had taken it back... in the process of reclaiming it, he had licked his finger, licked the book, then licked his finger again.

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti is a drunk poet who sold his worthless poetry to fund a new library and was dismissed by Sylvira as incapable of the murder’s planning.
source_quote: A drunk who is bitter... too much of a drunk to pull off something like that.

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti is a drunken poet who sells his worthless work to fund a new library; Sylvira dismissed him as too unskilled to orchestrate the framing, labeling him possible but unlikely.
source_quote: He's too much of a drunk to pull off something like that.

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti is referenced by Sylvira as the one whose research was dismissed as third-rate at best, and whose present was used as the vehicle for the poison.
source_quote: He was a clown, a boar, and his research was third-rate at best. Daral's present, unwrapped and coated in midnight tears

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti was the intended recipient of the poisoned book, which Alkrist planned to frame. Sylvira dismissed his work as inferior, suggesting he lacked the capability or credibility to carry out the murder himself.
source_quote: Daral: motive, but dismissed on execution grounds by someone who knew his work.

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral was dismissed by Sylvira as a practitioner whose work she knew well; his motive is plausible but execution deemed implausible by her.
source_quote: The same confident dismissal she'd given Daral: she knew her field.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes the only price he is interested in collecting is what A'lai knows about whoever is paying Menzoberranzan rates to keep him alive.
source_quote: And what he knows about whoever is paying Menzoberranzan rates to keep a nobody drow evoker alive and functional: that is the only price I am interested in collecting.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes the patron entry has receded every time he thought he was close to identifying it.
source_quote: Every time I thought I was close to something, it receded.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz considers A'lai the first real lead he's been offered since Kaelira laid out the problem.
source_quote: Now there was a compromised drow scholar who might represent the first real lead I'd been offered since Kaelira laid the problem out for me plainly.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz finds it uncomfortable to be the unknown variable in his own accounts.
source_quote: It is not comfortable to be the unknown variable in your own accounts.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz has an alternative proposal forming: A'lai should pay not in gold or books, but in knowledge about who is funding his protection.
source_quote: I had an alternative proposal forming. It was not finalized. But the terms were these: A'lai does not pay in gold, and does not pay in books. A'lai pays in what he knows.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz has been maintaining a column since Kaelira told him someone powerful was paying to protect a man he couldn't understand, and the entry remains blank.
source_quote: The column I had been maintaining since Kaelira told me bluntly that someone powerful was paying to protect a man she couldn't understand. That column had one entry, and I still couldn't name the entity.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a drow investigator assigned to interview Sylvira; he is skilled at extracting testimony, understands Menzoberranzan psychological tactics, and successfully navigated Sylvira’s trauma and suspicion to elicit critical information.
source_quote: Happy to talk to Sylvira in the meantime, or whoever can.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a drow investigator chosen to interview Sylvira due to his skill in eliciting testimony.
source_quote: Daz was the natural choice for it: he knew how to make someone talk, and he was drow, which was not irrelevant given what we knew about the Menzoberranzan thread running under all of this.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the investigator who concluded the case, compiled the full confession, and recognized that the true danger lay not in the actors but in the collective decision-making of those who had already decided Janussi’s fate.
source_quote: We had what we needed.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz knew Sylvira was not lying about her innocence and was genuinely seeking justice.
source_quote: You're right, you're right. We must focus on the problem at hand — capturing the person who murdered my love, and who is impersonating me.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz needs information from A'lai, given A'lai's drow connections and knowledge of the conspiracy.
source_quote: A'lai, moreover, is a drow. He might have information that Daz needs.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed Sylvira associated Kazryn Nyantani with deep resentment toward Janussi.
source_quote: Kazryn Nyantani. The name arrived with a weight that told me it had been sitting just below the surface.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed Sylvira was distressed when recalling her last words with Janussi.
source_quote: Those were my last words with him.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed Sylvira was using a mage hand despite being bedridden and shuddering.
source_quote: A mage hand, which was interesting: she was bedridden and shuddering under a fever, and still running a familiar and a mage hand from across the room.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observed that Sylvira felt relief beneath her shock and fear.
source_quote: Underneath both was something she hadn't meant to let through: relief.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized Sylvira believed her relationship with Janussi had made her a target.
source_quote: The relationship with Janussi had probably offended someone else on top of that.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized Sylvira was not incapacitated despite her fever.
source_quote: I filed that in the column marked *not incapacitated.*

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognizes that A'lai's knowledge is the most reliably underpriced resource in the world, especially when someone desperately needs discretion.
source_quote: I will not call it a commodity exactly. I will call it the most reliably underpriced resource in the world, especially in the hands of someone who desperately needs it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood Sylvira was being framed and that her accusation was a trick of perception.
source_quote: You're not aware that your likeness has been seen moving around, doing things you couldn't possibly have done?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz understood Sylvira was willing to collaborate fully with the investigation.
source_quote: I'm willing to collaborate with anything, and I'm delighted — delighted — that you are leading the investigation.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was the natural choice for the interview with Sylvira. He knew how to make someone talk, and he was drow, which was not irrelevant given what we knew about the Menzoberranzan thread running under all of this.
source_quote: Daz was the natural choice for it: he knew how to make someone talk, and he was drow, which was not irrelevant given what we knew about the Menzoberranzan thread running under all of this.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz's training runs toward knowing where every debt is, who holds it, and what it costs.
source_quote: My training ran toward the opposite: know where every debt is, who holds it, what it costs.

subject: Elian
fact: Elian believes that even an unsolved case can yield value if documented as a methodological contribution, and that scholarly endorsement has intrinsic worth.
source_quote: Even if we failed to solve the murder, even if all I could write was that these techniques would have helped, the academic community would still approve.

subject: Elian
fact: Elian believes that magical solutions like Speak with Dead are unreliable because the dead retain their motivations, biases, and performances, and that evidence must be gathered from multiple non-magical sources.
source_quote: Too many people... think: cast a spell, find the murderer. It doesn't work that way. ... They're still themselves. They forget, misattribute, have things they'd rather believe about what happened.

subject: Elian
fact: Elian is a Candlekeep scholar who champions epistemological rigor in criminal investigation, rejects the myth of the dead as transparent narrators, and seeks academic prestige through association with figures of stature — even if it means misrepresenting the nature of authorship.
source_quote: Too many people, if you ask me, think: cast a spell, find the murderer. It doesn't work that way.

subject: Elian
fact: Elian is a scholar at Candlekeep who argues that magic creates adversarial evidence and promotes the principle that facts must converge from multiple angles to be trusted.
source_quote: Elian said the paper had a whole section on it: the myth of the person. ... You cannot rely on magic to make evidence meaningful. It makes evidence adversarial. Collect facts from different angles: physical, testimonial, procedural.

subject: Elian
fact: Elian proposed collaboration on a monograph, initially misstating the role, then clarifying he would write it with Thorin contributing an introduction.
source_quote: Elian said having someone of my stature involved would do wonders for criminal investigation across Faerûn.

subject: Elian
fact: Elian referenced a document describing the 'myth of the person" — the false assumption that the dead shed their performances and tell pure truth — and later reached for another document, signaling an unresolved line of inquiry.
source_quote: The myth of the person. I'll have to look at it.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris is hunting Kalan Strongbranch to enable the Alkrist interview with binding evidence.
source_quote: I'm gonna have to hunt Kalan down," he said, the energy of a man who locates missing First Readers as a matter of routine.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris is the investigator tasked with locating Kalan Strongbranch, recognizing his critical role in validating the investigation’s framework; he operates with monastic precision and relentless focus.
source_quote: I'm gonna have to hunt Kalan down.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer arrived with notes and theories, emotionally and intellectually moved by the colloquium. He sought to collaborate on a written work, and ultimately handed his materials to Glabbagool, unaware that the gelatinous cube was the designated recipient.
source_quote: He handed them over. Glabbagool examined them with professional detachment: the focused, slightly acidic attention he gives to anything he's evaluating for nutritional content.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is a man who arrived rehearsing in the corridor, brought notes, and offered theories moved by the colloquium, intending to deposit them with Glabbagool.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer arrived. He came in like a man who'd been rehearsing in the corridor. Trying not to make an entrance. Making one anyway. He had notes.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is an ambitious academic who seeks institutional validation through co-authored monographs, misreads the nature of scholarly contribution, and is visibly disoriented when his intellectual labor is handed to non-human entities.
source_quote: He suggested a duograph. I allowed that this was possible: a dual log, perhaps, something in that register.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer, a dragonborn, immediately took initiative to locate Kalan Strongbranch, the First Reader who cast the truth-seeking spell, demonstrating a monastic commitment to urgent dispatch without hesitation or friction.
source_quote: I'm gonna have to hunt Kalan down... At some point I'll return with Kalan.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool believes he can eat through walls.
source_quote: Walls don't stop us. I can eat through walls

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool confirmed he can eat through walls and gaps, distinguishing between those that admit a gelatinous cube and those that do not.
source_quote: Glabbagool had made the distinction between a gap that admitted a gelatinous cube and a gap that did not.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool declared the notes inedible and stated 'This is not food,' with a quality of genuine longing, revealing emotional depth beyond mere function.
source_quote: 'This is not nutritious.' ... 'This is not food.' Then, with a quality of genuine longing I was not expecting: 'I remember when there was cheese.'

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool distinguishes between gaps that admit him and gaps that do not, demonstrating precise spatial awareness and self-knowledge.
source_quote: Glabbagool had made the distinction between a gap that admitted a gelatinous cube and a gap that did not.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool expressed genuine longing for cheese, a memory that is real and consistent, and whose emotional authenticity is not performed but deeply held.
source_quote: I remember when there was cheese. Perhaps if we had some cheese.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool grieves the loss of cheese.
source_quote: Perhaps if we had some cheese

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a gelatinous cube whose emotional life includes a genuine longing for cheese, and whose declarations of inedibility are not mechanical but deeply felt.
source_quote: I remember when there was cheese. Perhaps if we had some cheese.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a gelatinous cube with genuine, unperformed emotions — particularly a deep, nostalgic grief for cheese. He evaluates all input with nutritional precision and has consistently rejected non-nutritive materials, yet accepts them as part of his function.
source_quote: This is not nutritious. ... I remember when there was cheese. Perhaps if we had some cheese.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a gelatinous cube with profound, unperformed emotional depth — particularly regarding food, especially cheese — and possesses an unerring, literal capability to consume nearly any solid material, including walls and safes, which he states with calm, unshakable authority.
source_quote: Walls don't stop us. I can eat through walls. ... I remember when there was cheese. Perhaps if we had some cheese.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is referenced by the narrator as the one who observed Alkrist's interrogation without being asked to, and noted his collapse under truth.
source_quote: Glabbagool was in the room with us, settled near the far wall. He had been there since the beginning. I had not asked him to pay attention. He simply did

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool possesses a deep, non-performative emotional life, centered on the memory of cheese, and his grief is real and consistent.
source_quote: I remember when there was cheese. Perhaps if we had some cheese.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool possesses the ability to eat through walls and safe doors, and has never been wrong about what he can consume.
source_quote: Walls don't stop us. I can eat through walls. ... He has never been wrong about what he can eat.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool remembers when there was cheese.
source_quote: I remember when there was cheese

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool’s declaration 'This is not food' and his longing for cheese are treated as authentic emotional expressions, not mechanical outputs.
source_quote: 'This is not food.' Then, with a quality of genuine longing I was not expecting: 'I remember when there was cheese.'

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool’s emotional authenticity — particularly his grief over lost cheese — is more reliable than any testimony or magical detection, and his physical capabilities are absolute: walls, safes, and doors are merely temporary barriers to his nature.
source_quote: I remember when there was cheese. Perhaps if we had some cheese.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool’s emotional response to cheese is consistent, real, and treated as a core truth by Grygum, despite his non-human nature.
source_quote: I remember when there was cheese. Perhaps if we had some cheese.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum accepts that Glabbagool’s ability to eat through walls is a valid investigative tool, and that it was available all along, even if not used.
source_quote: He had simply offered a service that had, in retrospect, been available all along, and noted for the record that walls present no meaningful obstacle to his methodology.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the crime required calm, preparation, and patience, and that the perpetrator had planned for what happened after Janussi was dead.
source_quote: That is the kind of detail that belongs in a file you keep very carefully.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes Janussi had high intelligence but not high wisdom.
source_quote: Well, it's clear he may have high intelligence, but not high wisdom," Grygum said.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes that Glabbagool’s emotional consistency — particularly his grief over cheese — is a truth more reliable than any testimony.
source_quote: I find this, privately, both moving and correct.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes that the ground underfoot is the only fixed truth, and that magic is just another moving surface that must be triangulated against physical and testimonial facts.
source_quote: In the Underdark, the one thing that didn't lie was terrain. ... Magic was just another moving surface. The facts underneath it were still fixed.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes that the truth is fixed and that the investigator’s role is to assemble its picture from multiple converging facts, not to rely on magic or convenience.
source_quote: The truth doesn't change. What happened, happened. You're assembling a picture of something already fixed, not hunting something fluid.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes that truth does not change, and that the investigator’s role is to assemble a picture of something already fixed, not to hunt something fluid.
source_quote: The truth doesn't change. What happened, happened. You're assembling a picture of something already fixed, not hunting something fluid.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes the record of the quadrangle issue now exists and matters, regardless of whether Bahamut reads it.
source_quote: the record now exists, and the record says: the quadrangle issue landed

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum claims to have invented the phrase 'Once you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however unlikely, must be the truth,' though he has heard it before, and defends it as his contribution to the afternoon.
source_quote: 'Once you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however unlikely, must be the truth?' ... 'Yes,' Grygum said, with tremendous dignity. 'I made it up myself.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum intended to investigate the third-story apartment in Janussi's chambers.
source_quote: I'm gonna go look into that.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum introduced blackmail as an agenda item and noted that in murder mysteries, someone often treats blackmail as a kind of career, aligning with A'lai's profile.
source_quote: We could always decide to blackmail one or more of them... you often find somebody who treats blackmail as a kind of career.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a methodical investigator who values empirical convergence over magical shortcuts, carries deep institutional memory from the Underdark, and privately recognizes emotional authenticity in others — especially in Glabbagool — despite his own stoicism.
source_quote: I have carried this cube from the Underdark through several extremely dangerous situations, and his feelings about cheese are among the most consistent things about him.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a seasoned, calm arbiter who manages chaos with bureaucratic precision. He recognizes the emotional weight of others' contributions, accepts absurdity as part of the process, and delegates non-nutritive materials to Glabbagool without surprise.
source_quote: Deposit them with my secretary." ... "I meant it in the way one means things that have been settled administratively.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is investigating the third-story apartment and discovered Janussi’s critical review of Kalan’s proposal.
source_quote: Grygum headed upstairs for the physical evidence.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by Fembris Lancer as the authority whose position on the quadrangle issue was a brilliant insight that dramatically transformed the understanding of the case.
source_quote: Grygum, that was fantastic!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by the narrator as the one who recovered the wrapping paper and used Bahamut's cantrip to restore it to its original state.
source_quote: I turned it over in my hands... Bahamut's domain is... a cantrip that restores things to their original state... The paper did the rest

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the investigator who ascended to Janussi’s third-story apartment and uncovered the academic manuscript that revealed Janussi’s contemptuous rejection of Kalan’s methodology — a discovery that recontextualized the entire investigation.
source_quote: I'll head up and check that out.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the narrative architect — the one who introduces agenda items ('We could always decide to blackmail one or more of them') and who recognizes the administrative framing of murder. He is attuned to the irony of using bureaucratic language to mask violence.
source_quote: We could always decide to blackmail one or more of them.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the note in Janussi's chambers and read it.
source_quote: Oh, a note! I read it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum privately acknowledges that his stature is built on falling first, recalling Velkynvelve, and that he does not believe in magic as a substitute for observation.
source_quote: I thought briefly about Velkynvelve, which is where this all started: a dwarf in the wrong place, in chains, at the bottom of the world. Whatever stature looked like from the outside, it was built on a lot of falling first.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum privately finds Glabbagool's feelings about cheese both moving and correct.
source_quote: I find this, privately, both moving and correct

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum privately finds Glabbagool’s grief over cheese both moving and correct, and carries the cube’s emotional consistency as a truth more reliable than testimony.
source_quote: I find this, privately, both moving and correct.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum proposed the principle that 'once you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however unlikely, must be the truth,' and claimed to have invented it, though the speaker has heard it before in something read long ago.
source_quote: I made it up myself.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized Janussi had dismissed Kalan Strongbranch's proposal as solipsism.
source_quote: Janussi had reviewed Kalan Strongbranch's proposal for new criminal investigation methodologies, found it to be solipsism, and had blocked it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled that in murder mysteries, someone often treats blackmail as a kind of career.
source_quote: In these murder mysteries," Grygum said, "you often find somebody who treats blackmail as a kind of career.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled the wrapping paper from the poisoned book had been taken to the third-story apartment in Janussi's chambers.
source_quote: We knew the wrapping paper from the poisoned book had been taken there, and we hadn't gone back.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalls having had someone like Daral in their party before — someone who left after being healed.
source_quote: didn't we have somebody like that with our party anyhow? Did we already send him away?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum remembered that Alkrist had burned something at the feast.
source_quote: When you talk to Alkrist, there's something in the list about what Alkrist burned at the feast — you should ask about that.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum understood that Kalan had built his entire methodology in the wreckage of Janussi's contempt.
source_quote: Kalan's entire proposal for dealing with crime... had been buried under one man's contemptuous signature.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was the investigator who discovered Janussi's damning notes on the third floor of his chambers. He recognized the academic tone of contempt toward Kalan and filed the evidence, noting its implications for the investigation.
source_quote: Grygum was already moving for the stairs. He stopped, turned back. He'd remembered something.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi is Sylvira's former romantic partner, previously involved with Kazryn Nyantani, and their relationship with Sylvira has likely offended someone, contributing to her being targeted.
source_quote: Then Sylvira. Then...

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi is referenced by Alkrist as the one who dismissed his germ warfare research and denied him leadership potential.
source_quote: The performance review with Janussi: dismissed, told his germ warfare research was dangerous and should be stopped, told he showed no leadership potential

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi spent his last day in a library full of people who had already decided they'd won, and offered each of them one more reason on his way through — he was dead by midnight.
source_quote: Janussi had spent his last day in a library full of people who had already decided, and he had offered each of them one more reason on his way through.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a librarian at Candlekeep who systematically provoked Alkrist, A'lai, and Bookwyrm into wanting him dead by firing them, canceling their research, and trashing their work—all on the same day, culminating in his assassination.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a scholar and Keeper of Candlekeep who was murdered after opening a gift-wrapped book laced with poison. The murder was premeditated, not opportunistic, and the perpetrator planned for Janussi's death and its aftermath.
source_quote: The gift wrap for the deadly book. Someone had planned this: got the poison, picked the target, wrapped it up clean enough that a Keeper of Candlekeep... never noticed. Had opened it. Had thanked whoever sent it, maybe. Had been pleased.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a scholar of high intelligence but low wisdom — a man whose knowledge made him a target. His death was not random but strategic, and his research was destroyed not out of malice but to erase evidence of his own dangerous insights. He is the casualty of a system that rewards silence over truth.
source_quote: Well, it's clear he may have high intelligence, but not high wisdom.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was killed; Sylvira described him as a skilled Keeper of Tomes, and recalled their final argument was over a private matter, not any insult to his character.
source_quote: He was right to want him gone. He was a clown, a boar, and his research was third-rate at best.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was the victim of murder. His private notes revealed a pattern of academic contempt, particularly toward Kalan Strongbranch, whom he characterized as pursuing criminal investigation as a vanity project. His notes were found on the third floor of his chambers, alongside evidence of his personal habits and the wrapping paper from the poisoned book.
source_quote: The paper that had wrapped the poisoned book had been brought here, and nobody had retrieved it. Evidence doesn't improve with age.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was the victim who, on his final day, delivered verdicts that gave Alkrist, Bookwyrm, and A'lai separate and uncoordinated reasons to want him dead, effectively turning his own authority into a weapon against himself.
source_quote: He had walked from room to room delivering verdicts, and by midnight he was dead.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira told the investigator bluntly that someone powerful was paying to protect a man she couldn't understand, initiating the months-long column with one blank entry.
source_quote: Kaelira told me bluntly that someone powerful was paying to protect a man she couldn't understand.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is a spellcaster positioned outside the interrogation room, actively maintaining a truth spell on Alkrist. His presence ensures Alkrist cannot lie, though Alkrist is currently unaware of this.
source_quote: Kalan was outside the door. As of right now, Alkrist could not lie. He didn't know that yet.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is the wronged party with standing and motivation to be thorough. He is the one who asked the pivotal question: 'What do you do with the evidence you've collected?' His moral authority anchors the group’s ethical pivot from justice to strategic silence.
source_quote: Kalan was the party who had been wronged, Kalan had standing, Kalan was presumably motivated to be thorough.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan was the man fired by Janussi and subsequently framed as the scapegoat; he now holds the most complete account of the conspiracy and is the logical candidate to clean up the aftermath, though his standing makes him a potential pawn or target.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan was the party who had been wronged, had standing, and was presumably motivated to be thorough — he was the one fired and now held a complete account.
source_quote: Kalan had been standing just outside through all of it, which meant the man who'd been fired now held a rather complete account.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is referenced by Sylvira as the one who proposed insane investigative controls that Bookwyrm opposed.
source_quote: Kalan's proposal, which she called insane, all sorts of investigative controls and restrictions

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is the First Reader who developed the Threefold Proof methodology, which Janussi dismissed as solipsism.
source_quote: Kalan Strongbranch. The First Reader. The one with the truth-seeking spell that had already anchored the investigation once.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is the First Reader whose criminal investigation methodology, the Threefold Proof, was rejected and dismissed as solipsism by Janussi; he later presented the same framework to the investigation team, embedding his personal motive within institutional procedure.
source_quote: Who can cast the truth spell? Yeah — Kalan Strongbranch.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch sought Sylvira’s intervention to preserve his position under Janussi, but was rejected. Sylvira dismissed him as a 'clown' and implied his research was third-rate, suggesting a personal animosity that may have motivated retaliation.
source_quote: Janussi was right to want him gone. He was a clown, a boar, and his research was third-rate at best.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch's proposal for new criminal investigation methodologies was reviewed and dismissed by Janussi as solipsism, blocking it entirely. Kalan later presented that same framework as his operating methodology to the investigation team, despite having been publicly ridiculed by the victim.
source_quote: Janussi had reviewed Kalan Strongbranch's proposal for new criminal investigation methodologies, found it to be solipsism, and had blocked it. He wasn't interested, he wrote, in creating all these rules and procedures so that Kalan could go detect a murder mystery.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch, the First Reader, is the only known caster of the truth-seeking spell that previously anchored the investigation, and his current whereabouts are unknown, making him critical to resolving the current contradictions.
source_quote: Who can cast the truth spell? Yeah — Kalan Strongbranch.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan had petitioned Sylvira to intercede with Janussi to keep his job; Sylvira dismissed him as incompetent and never brought up the request.
source_quote: He was a clown, a boar, and his research was third-rate at best.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn Nyantani harbors a credible, long-standing resentment toward Sylvira, with apparent capability to act on it.
source_quote: Resentment credible enough to survive scrutiny, long-standing grudge, apparent capability.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn Nyantani is a former partner of Janussi, now bitter toward Sylvira for replacing her; Sylvira broke down acknowledging Kazryn’s resentment and implied personal guilt over the situation.
source_quote: That bitter old hag... who always resented Janussi for ditching her in favor of me.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn Nyantani was Janussi’s former lover and resented Sylvira for replacing her.
source_quote: That bitter old hag... who always resented Janussi for ditching her in favor of me.

subject: Leuwin
fact: Leuwin was helping A'lai in the garden at the Oak Tree Apothecary when a dragonborn arrived, as witnessed by Nibbles the squirrel.
source_quote: While Leuwin was helping A'lai in the garden, a dragonborn had arrived: a huge, lizard-skinned figure, per the testimony of Nibbles the squirrel.

subject: Narrator (Dragonborn)
fact: The narrator intended to use the dragonborn connection to open a conversation with Alkrist.
source_quote: I don't know if Alkrist would use it. I knew I could.

subject: Narrator (Dragonborn)
fact: The narrator noticed Fembris operated with monastic commitment to immediate tasks.
source_quote: There is something almost monastic about how Fembris operates: the total commitment to the immediate task, no friction between decision and movement.

subject: Narrator (Dragonborn)
fact: The narrator noticed the quality of conversation between dragonborn removes a layer of introduction and performance.
