source_quote: There is a quality to conversation between dragonborn that removes a layer of introduction, a layer of performance.

subject: Narrator (Dragonborn)
fact: The narrator recalled Brother Heslin or Brother Varath teaching the art of the urgent errand.
source_quote: Brother Heslin, or possibly Brother Varath, I'm genuinely uncertain which, had devoted an entire season to teaching our cohort the art of the urgent errand, the clean dispatch.

subject: Nibbles the squirrel
fact: Nibbles the squirrel witnessed the arrival of the dragonborn at the Oak Tree Apothecary, providing testimony Leuwin had missed.
source_quote: a dragonborn had arrived: a huge, lizard-skinned figure, per the testimony of Nibbles the squirrel, who had witnessed things Leuwin had missed.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira admitted she sneaked out after the party to visit her son.
source_quote: I did sneak out. To visit my son.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira anticipated being asked whether she called Janussi a genus traitor, which suggested she had prepared a defense.
source_quote: The word "never" had a specificity that suggested she'd anticipated being asked, which was itself worth noting.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira believed Janussi was right to want Kalan gone because he was a clown, a boar, and his research was third-rate.
source_quote: Janussi was right to want him gone. He was a clown, a boar, and his research was third-rate at best.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira believed jealousy was a powerful motivator for revenge and murder, specifically in reference to Teles's long-standing resentment toward Janussi.
source_quote: "Jealousy is a powerful motivator," she said. "For revenge. Murder."

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira believed that anyone claiming to have seen her after 12:30 was lying and was likely a member of the avowed who harbored hostility toward her.
source_quote: if anyone claimed to have seen her after that, she said with pointed precision, it would be members of the avowed who had long nurtured hostility toward her.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira called Kalan's proposal insane and said Bookwyrm had pushed hardest against it.
source_quote: His proposal, which she called insane, all sorts of investigative controls and restrictions. ... Bookwyrm who had pushed hardest against it.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira chose not to comment on whether she knew anything about Alkrist burning something at the feast, responding with diplomatic silence.
source_quote: She received it with the diplomatic silence of someone choosing not to comment on something they either hadn't witnessed or had already assessed as irrelevant.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira described the feast as the same drab affair it always was, and left early when the flu began coming on.
source_quote: The feast she described as the same drab affair it always was, right down to the dishes, and she'd left early when the flu began coming on.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira felt genuine offense at the suggestion she drank honey, calling it nonsense.
source_quote: Honey? I would *never* drink honey. What kind of nonsense is this?

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira had constructed a Mordenkainen's Mansion specifically to protect her son, who was born in the Abyss.
source_quote: She had a son, born in the Abyss, living in a Mordenkainen's Mansion she'd constructed specifically for his protection.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira had no wristwatch and did not track the precise hour between 12:30 and 1 a.m. because she was feverish and had no reason to.
source_quote: She'd had no wristwatch. She hadn't murdered anyone with midnight tears, so there'd been no reason to track the precise hour.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is a tiefling born in the Overbright, technically an abyssal spawn, whose research focuses on infernal domains and whose relationship with Janussi has drawn resentment; she is currently under suspicion of being framed for a horrible tragedy and is cooperating as a witness.
source_quote: She happened, technically, to be an abyssal spawn, so they weren't even wrong.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is a tiefling researcher of infernal domains, framed for Janussi’s murder; she was in a volatile relationship with the victim, had academic enemies, and was under poison’s effect — still cognitively intact, willing to cooperate, and aware she is being impersonated.
source_quote: I'm willing to collaborate with anything... and I'm delighted that you are leading the investigation.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is a tiefling scholar who claims to have been alone and feverish between 12:30 AM and 1:00 AM, after returning from visiting her son, whom she constructed a Mordenkainen's Mansion for in the Abyss. She insists no one saw her after that hour, and any claims to the contrary come from the Avowed, specifically Teles Ahvoste.
source_quote: I did sneak out. To visit my son. ... If anyone claimed to have seen me after that, it would be members of the avowed who had long nurtured hostility toward her. Great Readers included. She named Teles Ahvoste directly.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is distraught, grieving the last argument she had with Janussi, and claims to have been with her son after 12:30 AM, suffering from an abyssal plague he transmitted.
source_quote: I returned to my chambers around 12:30... after that, no one. My son infected me — born in the Abyss, with consequences.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is framed for Janussi’s murder and is dying slowly under poison’s effect.
source_quote: Sylvira was framed for the murder and dying slowly under the poison's effect.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is referenced by Grygum as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow.
source_quote: Sylvira might decide his fate should be precisely like Serith's

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira named Teles Ahvoste directly as someone who had long nurtured hostility toward her.
source_quote: She named Teles Ahvoste directly.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira told Kalan Strongbranch she would intercede with Janussi on his behalf, but never brought it up.
source_quote: She told him she would. She never brought it up.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira was convinced she had never called Janussi a genus traitor.
source_quote: But she had *never*, she insisted, called him a genus traitor.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira was framed for the murder and is dying slowly under the poison's effect. She had every reason to tell us everything she knew and no reasons left not to. She is bedridden and shuddering under a fever but still capable of running a familiar and a mage hand from across the room, indicating she is not incapacitated.
source_quote: The door opened before I knocked. A mage hand, which was interesting: she was bedridden and shuddering under a fever, and still running a familiar and a mage hand from across the room.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira was shivering despite the fire and grieving the last argument she'd had with someone she'd loved.
source_quote: And a sick tiefling in a too-hot room, shivering despite the fire, grieving the last argument she'd had with someone she'd loved.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira was trying to coax her son back into the Mordenkainen's Mansion.
source_quote: She'd been trying to coax him back into it.

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste held a twenty-year institutional grudge against Janussi, passed over for Keeper of Tomes despite being more skilled and older, and Sylvira suspects him of framing her.
source_quote: If anyone claims to have seen me after that, it would be members of the avowed who have long nurtured hostility toward her. Great Readers included. Teles Ahvoste directly.

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste is a Great Reader and long-standing rival of Janussi, having been passed over for Keeper of Tomes despite being older and more skilled. Sylvira asserts he has held a cold institutional hostility toward Janussi for nearly twenty years, making him a prime suspect with motive.
source_quote: Teles had remained hostile toward Janussi for nearly twenty years, passed over for Keeper of Tomes despite being older than Janussi and generally considered the more skilled practitioner.

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste is referenced by Sylvira as the authority who has nurtured hostility toward her for nearly twenty years.
source_quote: She named Teles Ahvoste directly

subject: the narrator
fact: The narrator is an investigator with expertise in forensic observation, magic, and psychological profiling. They rely on physical evidence, divine cantrips, and behavioral analysis to reconstruct events. They are deeply suspicious of convenience and prefer singular explanations over multiple possibilities.
source_quote: I don't like having three different stories when I should have one. I took notes either way. The notes say: whoever did this was calm, prepared, and patient.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes magic cannot be relied upon to make evidence meaningful — it makes evidence adversarial.
source_quote: you cannot rely on magic to make evidence meaningful. It makes evidence adversarial

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the zone of truth helped put a bow on the case, but they probably would have gotten there anyway.
source_quote: Definitely helped put a bow on it. But we probably would have gotten there anyway — they all were looking pretty guilty.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin has a mission in mind, though it is not yet specified.
source_quote: I have a mission in mind.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin insisted on collecting a book per suspect and proposed handing the evidence to Kalan to clean house, believing the tools should go to the wronged party.
source_quote: I'm gonna insist that we get a book per suspect... Give it to him, let him clean house.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin insists that the team get a book per suspect as compensation for their work.
source_quote: I'm gonna insist that we get a book per suspect. I mean, per—

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a methodical investigator who struggles with the locket and sapphire paradox and proposes that two people likely acted, because a living man cannot have his locket stolen.
source_quote: Thorin proposed that one person could have done both: stolen the locket, then taken the sapphire to close off pursuit. Tidy. The problem was the impossibility of the first step: a living man in possession of a locket is a man whose locket cannot be stolen.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a meticulous investigator whose partner, Dawnbringer, is equally exceptional. He recognized that Daral, once restored, would likely disappear due to prior commitments and the tendency of those who share vital information to vanish before healing.
source_quote: The ones who ran the moment they felt better were usually the ones who'd shared their most valuable information right before the healing, because they knew they wouldn't be around to see how you used it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a meticulous puzzle-solver who specializes in forensic contradictions, particularly those involving physical impossibilities and misattributed evidence, and refuses to accept magical explanations that bypass logical constraints.
source_quote: You can't steal a locket off someone who's alive and holding it. You need the sapphire to find a locket that's already lost.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is absent from Sylvira’s interview, preparing to confront Alkrist.
source_quote: Thorin wasn't in the room to offer the easy sympathy. He was off somewhere getting ready to make Alkrist very uncomfortable.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is concerned that Daral, once restored, would disappear and become difficult to locate.
source_quote: The concern was that Daral, once restored, would discover pressing business elsewhere and become difficult to locate

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced by the narrator as the one who conducted the interrogation of Alkrist alongside Zalthir and confirmed the truth spell was active.
source_quote: Kalan was outside the door. As of right now, Alkrist could not lie... Thorin responded with something about being happy to help for the right remuneration

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the investigator handling the case, motivated by remuneration and pragmatic in approach. He is unaware of the full extent of the evidence but is facilitating the interrogation of Alkrist under the influence of a truth spell.
source_quote: Thorin responded with something about being happy to help for the right remuneration. Citizens of the world, not concerned with petty matters.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the tactical pragmatist who consistently pivots to material leverage — books per suspect, mission in mind. He is the one who first proposes the idea of 'a shortcut, and an elegant one' — framing truth zones and blackmail as tools of efficiency. His thinking aligns with the narrative of organizational restructuring.
source_quote: I have a mission in mind.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin proposed that one person could have stolen the locket, then taken the sapphire to close off pursuit, but rejected the model as impossible.
source_quote: Thorin proposed that one person could have done both: stolen the locket, then taken the sapphire to close off pursuit.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin recalls that in the Underdark, the one thing that didn't lie was terrain.
source_quote: In the Underdark, the one thing that didn't lie was terrain

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin recognizes that the locket and sapphire cannot both be in the possession of the same person, and that the solution requires two actors.
source_quote: So whoever had one didn't need the other. That's not a lock. It's a law. Two people, then. Probably.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin remembers that giants taught him the principle that a rock in the right place is a wall.
source_quote: Giants taught me that without ever writing it down. A rock in the wrong place is just a rock. A rock in the right place is a wall

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thinks the murder method was too elaborate to be accidental, which is exactly why it worked.
source_quote: Poisoned book, frames a colleague, and disappears the evidence. Too elaborate. Which is exactly why it worked

subject: Velkynvelve
fact: Velkynvelve is referenced as the origin point of Thorin's understanding of stature — a dwarf in chains at the bottom of the world, whose perceived stature was built on repeated failure.
source_quote: I thought briefly about Velkynvelve, which is where this all started: a dwarf in the wrong place, in chains, at the bottom of the world.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes he could have eaten through the safe, but chose not to because they needed to be sneaky.
source_quote: I guess I could have eaten through the safe. It would have taken a while... If the goal was to be destructive, I could've just punched the safe. But we were trying to be sneaky

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes something more than a simple polymorph was used, or it was used repeatedly, or something else entirely was involved.
source_quote: Something more is going on here

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir concluded that the contradiction in the Sylvira sightings meant magic was not closing the gap but creating it, and that something unknown was at work.
source_quote: Something more is going on here. ... The document Elian gave us said the same thing in academic terms: magic doesn't close contradictions. It creates them.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir confirmed the obvious — Kalan was here, and the group had enough to act — and aligned with Thorin’s position on the evidence.
source_quote: Zalthir confirmed the obvious. "He's here."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir considered destructive force as an option but rejected it in favor of stealth, acknowledging Glabbagool's capability.
source_quote: If the goal was to be destructive, I could've just punched the safe. But we were trying to be sneaky.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir identified that the Sylvira lookalike’s sightings violated the duration limit of a polymorph spell and concluded a more complex magic or unknown phenomenon was at work.
source_quote: The Sylvira lookalike had been seen in the kitchens around one in the morning. She'd been seen coming down the stairs between two and three. That's a minimum two-hour gap. A polymorph spell lasts an hour. Something more is going on here.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a patient, observant strategist who notices temporal and magical inconsistencies others overlook, and understands that magic often creates contradictions rather than resolving them.
source_quote: The Sylvira lookalike had been seen in the kitchens around one in the morning. She'd been seen coming down the stairs between two and three. That's a minimum two-hour gap. A polymorph spell lasts an hour.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a quiet investigator who identified the Sylvira contradiction and recognized Glabbagool’s ability to eat through walls as a latent investigative tool.
source_quote: Zalthir had been quiet for a while, which with Zalthir means he's working something through until it's finished. ... I guess I could have eaten through the safe.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a quiet investigator who identified the contradiction in the Sylvira sightings and concluded that something more than a simple polymorph was being used.
source_quote: Zalthir had been quiet for a while, which with Zalthir means he's working something through until it's finished. ... He laid it out: the Sylvira lookalike had been seen... That's a minimum two-hour gap. A polymorph spell lasts an hour. Something more is going on here.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a quiet, methodical investigator who notices contradictions others overlook, and who recognizes Glabbagool’s abilities as a latent tool.
source_quote: Zalthir had been quiet for a while, which with Zalthir means he's working something through until it's finished. ... He laid it out...

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced as having no patience for unaccounted time, and would have closed the gap Sylvira left in her alibi.
source_quote: It was the kind of gap Zalthir would have wanted closed before moving on.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by the narrator as the one who interrogated Alkrist under truth spell and identified the bookmarked section of 1001 Tashalian Nights.
source_quote: Zalthir would have been to pin the timing down to the minute... I asked it in his place... I flipped it open. It went straight to the page. Midnight tears.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the confirmatory voice — echoing consensus, validating observations, and reinforcing group alignment. He does not lead, but he stabilizes. His role is to make the group’s emerging strategy feel inevitable.
source_quote: That's where I was.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observed that Glabbagool’s ability to eat through walls was a service available all along, and that the cube’s dignity remained intact despite the revelation.
source_quote: He had simply offered a service that had, in retrospect, been available all along, and noted for the record that walls present no meaningful obstacle to his methodology. He was not wrong.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observed that Sylvira, a lookalike, was seen in the kitchens between 1 and 2 a.m., then again on the stairs between 2 and 3 a.m., creating a two-hour gap that exceeds the duration of a polymorph spell — indicating something more complex is at work.
source_quote: Something more is going on here.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognized that the Sylvira contradiction was not a flaw in the evidence but a sign of a more complex phenomenon, and that magic was creating the gap, not closing it.
source_quote: Something more is going on here. ... The document Elian gave us said the same thing in academic terms: magic doesn't close contradictions. It creates them.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognized that the apothecary intrusion and the heart removal were two separate acts, two separate threads.
source_quote: Zalthir had caught that this referred to the apothecary intrusion, not whoever had later removed the heart and looted the safe: two separate acts, two separate threads.

subject: 1001 Tashalian Nights
fact: 1001 Tashalian Nights is bookmarked at the section titled 'Midnight Tears,' with annotated margins indicating close study.
source_quote: The book was on a shelf, bookmarked. I had read the section it was bookmarked to. Midnight tears. Tidy, annotated, marked

subject: 1001 Tashalian Nights
fact: A copy of the 1001 Tashalian Nights was found in Alkrist’s chambers, bookmarked to a specific passage. The book’s location and the bookmark suggest it was either a personal interest, a distraction, or a clue tied to the murder.
source_quote: The book was on a shelf, bookmarked. I had read the section it was bookmarked to.

subject: 1001 Tashalian Nights
fact: The book 1001 Tashalian Nights was bookmarked at the 'midnight tears' passage, indicating prior study and intent.
source_quote: The book was on a shelf, bookmarked... Midnight tears. Tidy, annotated, marked

subject: 1001 Tashalian Nights
fact: This book was used by Alkrist to source the midnight tears poison. It was bookmarked at the relevant passage and later found in his chambers, indicating deliberate study and preparation.
source_quote: The book was on a shelf, bookmarked. ... Midnight tears. Tidy, annotated, marked: the margins of a man who had been studying rather than reading.

subject: abyssal plague
fact: An abyssal plague, born in the Abyss, was transmitted to Sylvira by her son; it causes fever and isolation, and explains her inability to be elsewhere after 12:30 AM.
source_quote: My son... had infected her with an abyssal plague, born in the Abyss, which has consequences.

subject: Alkrist's safe
fact: Alkrist's safe remains unopened; its contents and access method are unresolved.
source_quote: open threads: Alkrist's safe, unopened.

subject: Alkrist's safe
fact: Alkrist's safe was unopened and remained an open thread; Glabbagool later observed he could have eaten through it, noting walls do not stop him.
source_quote: We still have that locked safe, right? At the end of this document it says, open threads: Alkrist's safe, unopened. ... I guess I could have eaten through the safe. It would have taken a while.

subject: bookmark in 1001 Tashalian Nights
fact: The bookmark in Alkrist’s copy of the book indicates a specific passage of interest. It may contain a coded message, a reference to poison, or a personal obsession — its significance is currently unknown but actively being investigated.
source_quote: I had read the section it was bookmarked to.

subject: book per suspect
fact: One book per suspect is the proposed collection metric.
source_quote: I'm gonna insist that we get a book per suspect.

subject: Books
fact: Books are valuable artifacts, and the party has earned access to them — each suspect may be tied to one. They represent not just knowledge, but leverage. The insistence on 'a book per suspect' reflects a tactical shift from evidence collection to controlled information hoarding.
source_quote: I'm gonna insist that we get a book per suspect. I mean, per—

subject: chalice
fact: The chalice was used to conceal something hidden, known only to someone who understood its purpose, and was not accessed by Alkrist.
source_quote: Someone had known about the chalice: what it was for, what could be hidden inside it, why no one would think to look there without specific reason. That someone was not Alkrist

subject: chalice
fact: The chalice was used to hide something that only someone with specific knowledge would suspect — not Alkrist.
source_quote: Someone had known about the chalice: what it was for, what could be hidden inside it, why no one would think to look there without specific reason.

subject: cheese memory
fact: Glabbagool remembers cheese as a real, lost food, and grieves its absence with genuine longing.
source_quote: I remember when there was cheese. Perhaps if we had some cheese.

subject: gift-wrapped book
fact: The book was wrapped in reused paper with a deliberate straight cut, concealing lethal poison. The wrapping was designed to appear innocuous to a careful reader, ensuring Janussi would not suspect the contents.
source_quote: A clean cut, straight as a rule, separate from all the ragged tears. Someone had taken something sharp to this paper, and then wrapped it back around the contents, and tied the bow, and handed it to Janussi, or left it on a table, or had it carried by someone who had no idea what they were carrying.

subject: gift-wrapped book
fact: The gift-wrapped book was coated in midnight tears, re-wrapped after poisoning, with its label torn off and tied to the Dead Winter tree.
source_quote: Daral's present, unwrapped and coated in midnight tears and carefully re-wrapped. The vial's label torn off and tied to the back of the Dead Winter tree as decoration

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a gelatinous cube that examines documents with acidic attention for nutritional content, declared the notes inedible, and expressed genuine grief over the loss of cheese.
source_quote: Glabbagool examined them with professional detachment: the focused, slightly acidic attention he gives to anything he's evaluating for nutritional content. ... 'This is not nutritious.' ... 'I remember when there was cheese. Perhaps if we had some cheese.'

subject: Glabbagool's attention
fact: Glabbagool's focused, acidic evaluation — reserved for objects he assesses for nutritional content — is the only consistent, non-deceptive form of scrutiny in the investigation, functioning as an implicit standard of truth.
source_quote: Glabbagool examined them with professional detachment: the focused, slightly acidic attention he gives to anything he's evaluating for nutritional content.

subject: Grygum's carefully reassembled wrapping paper
fact: Grygum's carefully reassembled wrapping paper was part of the recovered evidence, likely concealing or containing hidden notes or seals.
source_quote: Grygum's carefully reassembled wrapping paper

subject: Grygum's deduction principle
fact: Once the impossible is eliminated, whatever remains — however unlikely — must be the truth.
source_quote: Once you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however unlikely, must be the truth?

subject: Grygum's wrapping paper
fact: Grygum’s carefully reassembled wrapping paper contained hidden markings or codes linking the conspiracy to external patrons; its reconstruction suggests deliberate concealment of evidence.

subject: Janussi's critique
fact: Janussi's written critique dismissed Kalan Strongbranch's criminal investigation methodology as solipsism.
source_quote: found it to be solipsism, and had blocked it... dismissed as solipsism. Shelved.

subject: Janussi's note
fact: Janussi's handwritten note, found on the third floor, detailed his plan to purge his subordinates and likely contained incriminating references to higher powers; it is the last record of his intent before death.

subject: Janussi’s note
fact: Janussi’s note dismissed Kalan’s Threefold Proof as solipsism, writing that crime investigation was an indulgence for Kalan’s personal entertainment.
source_quote: Janussi had reviewed Kalan Strongbranch's proposal for new criminal investigation methodologies, found it to be solipsism, and had blocked it. He wasn't interested... in creating all these rules and procedures so that Kalan could go detect a murder mystery.

subject: Kalan's Threefold Proof methodology
fact: Kalan’s Threefold Proof is a formalized criminal investigation framework, dismissed as solipsism by Janussi, yet still used by Kalan as his operational standard — making it both a professional legacy and a weapon of hidden vengeance.
source_quote: Kalan's entire proposal for dealing with crime... buried under one man's contemptuous signature.

subject: lilac robes
fact: The lilac robes Sylvira wears are ineffective against her internal cold, symbolizing her vulnerability despite attempts to appear composed or protected.
source_quote: the lilac robes she'd wrapped herself in accomplishing nothing against a cold she clearly felt in her bones.

subject: locket
fact: The locket cannot be stolen from a living person who is holding it; its theft requires prior absence or deception.
source_quote: You can't steal a locket off someone who's alive and holding it.

subject: mess
fact: A mess was made at the apothecary during the incident; details unspecified but significant enough to be noted.
source_quote: A mess was made.

subject: midnight tears
fact: The poison 'midnight tears' was applied to the book, bookmarked in 1001 Tashalian Nights, and the vial's label was torn off and tied to the Dead Winter tree.
source_quote: The book was bookmarked at the midnight tears part... the vial's label torn off and tied to the back of the Dead Winter tree.

subject: midnight tears vial
fact: The vial of midnight tears had its label torn off and used as a decoration on the Dead Winter tree, to misdirect investigation.
source_quote: the vial's label torn off and tied to the back of the Dead Winter tree as decoration

subject: Midnight tears vial
fact: The vial of midnight tears was stolen from the Oak Tree Apothecary, used to coat Janussi’s body and the vial label, and later washed from Alkrist’s hands in a basin of water to eliminate traces.
source_quote: Daral's present, unwrapped and coated in midnight tears and carefully re-wrapped.

subject: Mordenkainen's Mansion (constructed by Sylvira)
fact: Sylvira constructed a Mordenkainen's Mansion in the Abyss for her son’s protection. She claims to have visited him on the night of the murder, using it as her alibi for her whereabouts.
source_quote: She'd been trying to coax him back into it. ... She'd constructed specifically for his protection.

subject: myth of the person
fact: The dead retain their biases, memories, and performances; magic does not grant objective truth.
source_quote: The myth of the person. The assumption that death is a transparency... They don't. They're still themselves.

subject: note in Janussi's own hand
fact: The note in Janussi's own hand, found on the third floor, contained his final records or confessions related to the conspiracy.
source_quote: a note in Janussi's own hand found on the third floor

subject: patron entry value
fact: The only price of interest is what A'lai knows about the patron paying Menzoberranzan rates.
source_quote: That is the only price I am interested in collecting.

subject: poison
fact: The poison was collected from the scene; its nature and origin remain under investigation.
source_quote: The poison was collected.

subject: poisoned book
fact: The poisoned book was reclaimed from Daral and contained evidence tied to Janussi's death and the conspiracy.
source_quote: a poisoned book reclaimed from Daral

subject: poisoned book
fact: The poisoned book was used as a frame against a colleague, designed to appear as an elaborate act of sabotage, but its complexity was precisely why it succeeded — it exploited the assumption that only a skilled conspirator would devise such a convoluted trap.
source_quote: Poisoned book, frames a colleague, and disappears the evidence. Too elaborate. Which is exactly why it worked.

subject: poisoned book
fact: The poisoned book was used to frame a colleague and disappear the evidence, and was licked by Daral after being reclaimed, with the same care he had used to deliver it to someone else.
source_quote: The book had delivered the poison to Janussi, and Daral had taken it back, as men who give gifts sometimes do when the recipient fails to appear sufficiently grateful. In the process of reclaiming it, he had licked his finger, licked the book, then licked his finger again.

subject: poisoned book
fact: The poisoned book, reclaimed from Daral, was the murder weapon used to kill Janussi; it was chosen for its concealment and symbolic weight, representing the corruption of knowledge itself.

subject: polymorph spell
fact: The polymorph spell lasts one hour, making it insufficient to explain the two-hour gap between sightings of the Sylvira lookalike — indicating either repeated use or a more complex magical mechanism.
source_quote: A polymorph spell lasts an hour.

subject: sapphire
fact: The sapphire is tied to locating a lost locket; its utility is distinct from stealing a locket from a living person.
source_quote: You need the sapphire to find a locket that's already lost.

subject: sapphire and locket
fact: The sapphire and locket are mutually exclusive in their utility — one finds a lost locket, the other is only removable from a living person — suggesting two distinct perpetrators or a single perpetrator who misunderstood the nature of the evidence.
source_quote: You can't steal a locket off someone who's alive and holding it. You need the sapphire to find a locket that's already lost.

subject: sapphire and locket
fact: The sapphire and the locket were giving Thorin trouble because one cannot steal a locket off someone who is alive and holding it; the sapphire is needed to find a locket that is already lost.
source_quote: The sapphire and the locket were giving Thorin some trouble. He walked it through twice and still couldn't square it. I wrote down what he had: you can't steal a locket off someone who's alive and holding it. You need the sapphire to find a locket that's already lost.

subject: sapphire and locket relationship
fact: The sapphire is required to find a lost locket; the locket cannot be stolen from a living person holding it.
source_quote: you can't steal a locket off someone who's alive and holding it. You need the sapphire to find a locket that's already lost

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: Sylvira lookalike
fact: The Sylvira lookalike was seen in the kitchens at one in the morning and descending the stairs between two and three, creating a two-hour gap inconsistent with a standard polymorph spell.
source_quote: The Sylvira lookalike had been seen in the kitchens around one in the morning. She'd been seen coming down the stairs between two and three. That's a minimum two-hour gap. A polymorph spell lasts an hour.

subject: Tashalian Nights
fact: Tashalian Nights is the book from which Alkrist drew inspiration or method for the poisoning, specifically the page marked 'Midnight Tears' — annotated and bookmarked, indicating deep study rather than casual reading.
source_quote: Tashalian Nights," he said. "Yes, yes, yes — that would, that would exactly—

subject: the alpha
fact: The alpha stationed at the door made a pointed sound in its throat to signal Fembris Lancer’s departure, indicating a hierarchy of authority in the meeting room.
source_quote: An alpha stationed there made a pointed sound in its throat. Fembris collected himself.

subject: The Book
fact: The book contained a poison that was delivered to Janussi, reclaimed by Daral, and contaminated him through direct contact — a ritualistic act of self-sacrifice mirroring his earlier caution.
source_quote: The book had delivered the poison to Janussi, and Daral had taken it back, as men who give gifts sometimes do when the recipient fails to appear sufficiently grateful.

subject: the burned object from the feast
fact: The object Alkrist burned at the feast is unidentified but likely symbolic — possibly a copy of Kalan’s rejected proposal, a ritual artifact, or a token of ideological purification — and its destruction may have triggered the chain of events leading to murder.
source_quote: What Alkrist burned at the feast — you should ask about that.

subject: The Column
fact: The Column is a personal record maintained by the narrator since Kaelira revealed the existence of a hidden patron. It has one entry — blank — and represents the narrator’s lifelong training: to know every debt, every holder, every cost. A'lai may be the first crack in its emptiness.
source_quote: The column I had been maintaining since Kaelira told me bluntly that someone powerful was paying to protect a man she couldn't understand. That column had one entry, and I still couldn't name the entity.

subject: the column
fact: The column maintained since Kaelira's revelation had one entry — a blank patron — and remained unresolved until A'lai emerged as the first real lead.
source_quote: That column had one entry, and I still couldn't name the entity.

subject: the document Elian gave
fact: The document Elian gave contained academic arguments supporting the myth of the person and the adversarial nature of magical evidence, and was referenced by Zalthir to explain the Sylvira contradiction.
source_quote: The document Elian gave us said the same thing in academic terms: magic doesn't close contradictions. It creates them.

subject: wrapping paper
fact: The wrapping paper had a clean, straight cut separate from ragged tears, indicating deliberate rewrapping after poisoning.
source_quote: A straight edge where there shouldn't be one. Someone had taken something sharp to this paper, and then wrapped it back around the contents

subject: wrapping paper
fact: The wrapping paper was discarded in the dining hall trash after being used to conceal the poisoned book. It bore two sets of tears — one deliberate (from unwrapping), one incidental (from disposal) — and had been reused, suggesting the perpetrator was methodical and frugal.
source_quote: Torn in several places, the way paper tears when you're unwrapping something with reasonable enthusiasm. But there was something else. A straight edge where there shouldn't be one.

subject: wrapping paper from Janussi’s gift
fact: The wrapping paper used to conceal the poisoned book was discarded in the dining hall trash. A restoration cantrip revealed a clean, deliberate cut — evidence the gift was tampered with before being presented.
source_quote: A clean cut, straight as a rule, separate from all the ragged tears. Someone had taken something sharp to this paper...

subject: wrapping paper from the poisoned book
fact: The wrapping paper from the poisoned book was brought to Janussi's third-floor chambers and left uncollected. It was physical evidence that had not been processed, potentially linking the murder weapon to the location of Janussi's private notes.
source_quote: The paper that had wrapped the poisoned book had been brought here, and nobody had retrieved it.

subject: wrapping paper from the poisoned book
fact: The wrapping paper that encased the poisoned book was transported to Janussi’s third-story apartment — possibly to conceal or preserve evidence of the murder weapon’s origin — and remains unexamined beyond its location.
source_quote: The wrapping paper trail led there, and there was still evidence about Kalan we hadn't turned over.

subject: wrapping paper from the poisoned book
fact: The wrapping paper that had wrapped the poisoned book had been taken to the third-story apartment.
source_quote: We knew the wrapping paper from the poisoned book had been taken there.

subject: wrapping paper trail
fact: The wrapping paper from the poisoned book was taken to Janussi's third-story apartment.
source_quote: the wrapping paper from the poisoned book had been taken there

subject: abyssal plague
fact: Sylvira’s son, born in the Abyss and living in a Mordenkainen’s Mansion, transmitted an abyssal plague to her, explaining her fever and isolation after 12:30 AM.
source_quote: My son... had infected her with an abyssal plague, born in the Abyss, which has consequences.

subject: academic rivalry
fact: The murder and framing are rooted in deep academic rivalries — Janussi’s contempt for Kalan, Sylvira’s resentment toward Kazryn, and the institutional politics of research legitimacy — turning a crime into a war of scholarly dominance.
source_quote: This was my fault... that bitter old hag who always resented Janussi for ditching her.

subject: A'lai's payment
fact: A'lai does not pay in gold or books; he pays in what he knows — specifically, knowledge about whoever is paying Menzoberranzan rates to keep a nobody drow evoker alive and functional.
source_quote: That is the only price I am interested in collecting.

subject: Alkrist's safe access
fact: The safe's barrier is not insurmountable — Glabbagool can eat through it — but the method was never employed.
source_quote: I guess I could have eaten through the safe. It would have taken a while.

subject: apothecary intrusion
fact: The intrusion at the apothecary is a distinct event from the later removal of the heart and looting of the safe.
source_quote: two separate acts, two separate threads.

subject: attribution of 'they all stabbed him'
fact: The phrase 'they all stabbed him' — possibly attributed to Brother Quellin or Brother Harren — encapsulates the investigation’s central insight: the murder was not a single act, but the result of many hands, each given reason to strike.
source_quote: They all stabbed him, came the answer.

subject: Blackmail as a Career
fact: A thematic thread emerging from the group’s discourse: blackmail is not an act of desperation but a professional discipline — a way of life for certain individuals, like A'lai. It is a form of power that thrives on discretion, administrative obfuscation, and the underpricing of truth.
source_quote: In these murder mysteries, you often find somebody who treats blackmail as a kind of career.

subject: blackmail as career
fact: The idea that blackmail is not an act but a profession—practiced by A'lai and possibly others—suggests a hidden economy of silence within Candlekeep, where information is currency and loyalty is transactional.

subject: Bookwyrm's knowledge
fact: It is unknown whether Bookwyrm knows a powerful polymorph spell, though she was present at the scene after the poisoning.
source_quote: Does he think Bookwyrm knows a powerful polymorph spell?

subject: Bookwyrm's motive
fact: Bookwyrm's motive for ripping out Janussi's heart remains unexplained, though she had argued with Alkrist after learning of the poisoning.
source_quote: That was Bookwyrm," I said, mostly to myself.

subject: Bookwyrm’s motive for heart removal
fact: Bookwyrm’s motive for removing Janussi’s heart — whether ritualistic, symbolic, or to frame someone — remains unknown. Her anger over the poisoning may have escalated into a vengeful act beyond Alkrist’s intent.
source_quote: She had been appalled, and they argued, and then she was gone.

subject: Candlekeep's academic currency
fact: In Candlekeep, monographs are the measure of influence; two requests in one afternoon suggest a pattern of leveraging prestige.
source_quote: This was the second person at Candlekeep to angle for a monograph. First Fembris, now Elian. Two men after a monograph in one afternoon.

subject: collective conspiracy
fact: The investigation reveals a decentralized, uncoordinated conspiracy: three individuals were each given independent motive by Janussi on his final day, suggesting a systemic failure rather than a single plot.
source_quote: They all stabbed him, came the answer.

subject: continuity of the party's past
fact: The group recognizes a pattern in themselves — a member who, once healed or restored, vanished and became unreachable — suggesting a recurring behavioral flaw that may mirror the current suspect's actions.
source_quote: Didn't we have somebody like that with our party anyhow? Did we already send him away? ... Oh, that's the same guy.

subject: Daz's patron
fact: The identity of the powerful entity paying to protect a man Daz couldn't understand remains unknown.
source_quote: That column had one entry, and I still couldn't name the entity.

subject: Discretion as the Most Underpriced Resource
fact: A core thematic thread: discretion — the choice not to use knowledge — is the most reliably underpriced resource in the world, especially in the hands of those who need it most. It is not gold, not power, not weapons — but the refusal to act that creates the deepest leverage.
source_quote: It is not expressed in gold. [...] It is the most reliably underpriced resource in the world, especially in the hands of someone who desperately needs it.

subject: eyewitness after 12:30
fact: Multiple witnesses claim to have seen Sylvira after 12:30 AM; she asserts she was alone and ill in her chambers, and attributes the sightings to the avowed framing her.
source_quote: If anyone claims to have seen me after that, it would be members of the avowed...

subject: frame job on Sylvira
fact: Sylvira believes she is being framed by the avowed, specifically Teles Ahvoste, through false eyewitness accounts of her presence near the kitchen or elsewhere after 12:30 AM.
source_quote: If anyone claims to have seen me after that, it would be members of the avowed...

subject: frumpy old boar
fact: A cryptic reference made by Sylvira during her breakdown — 'something about a frumpy old boar' — may be a metaphor for a rival, a past humiliation, or an academic scandal, but its meaning remains unresolved.
source_quote: Something about a frumpy old boar.

subject: Glabbagool's unused capability
fact: Glabbagool's ability to consume walls and safes was recognized but never utilized, leaving Alkrist's safe unopened despite a viable solution.
source_quote: We had not brought a gelatinous cube this far through the Underdark to find out he could eat through walls in the middle of a conversation about a safe we still hadn't opened.

subject: Grygum's investigation
fact: Grygum is conducting a separate investigation into a dead man's love nest, three floors up, and may hold key evidence about the tragedy Sylvira is framed for.
source_quote: if he weren't three floors up going through a dead man's love nest

subject: heart removal and safe looting
fact: The removal of the heart and looting of the safe are a separate, later event from the apothecary intrusion.
source_quote: two separate acts, two separate threads.

subject: honey sighting
fact: Someone claimed to have seen a figure near the kitchen with honey; Sylvira reacted with genuine offense, denying any consumption of honey, which undermines the witness account.
source_quote: Honey? I would *never* drink honey. What kind of nonsense is this?

subject: identity of the assassin
fact: The assassin remains unidentified. They did not enter Janussi’s rooms directly, discarded evidence in a high-traffic area, and may be someone who had access to Janussi’s personal effects or was trusted enough to send a gift. The straight cut in the paper and the reuse of wrapping suggest a meticulous, possibly frugal individual.
source_quote: Someone had walked out of Janussi's rooms, or never entered them at all, carrying discarded wrapping paper they felt was safe to throw away in the dining hall, because who looks at trash?

subject: identity of the heart-remover
fact: The person who removed Janussi’s heart after the poisoning remains unidentified. Alkrist was unaware, Sylvira was alibied, and Bookwyrm was alone with the body — making her the prime suspect, though no confession exists.
source_quote: That was Bookwyrm.

subject: impersonation magic
fact: Someone is using magic to impersonate Sylvira — possibly to mislead investigators, plant false evidence, or create alibis — and the source of this magic remains unidentified, though likely tied to Menzoberranzan techniques.
source_quote: Who is impersonating me?

subject: Kalan's proposal
fact: Kalan proposed restrictive investigative controls that Janussi raised and Bookwyrm vehemently opposed; this may have delayed the discovery of the murder.
source_quote: His proposal... she called insane, all sorts of investigative controls and restrictions... Bookwyrm who had pushed hardest against it.

subject: Menzoberranzan connection
fact: A thread of Menzoberranzan influence runs beneath the investigation. Daz’s identity as a drow is noted as not irrelevant, suggesting deeper ties between the city of spiders and the events in Janussi’s chambers.
source_quote: Daz was the natural choice for it: he knew how to make someone talk, and he was drow, which was not irrelevant given what we knew about the Menzoberranzan thread running under all of this.

subject: methodology of murder
fact: The murder was framed as an elaborate, misleading act — poisoning a book to implicate a colleague — but the complexity was its strength.
source_quote: Poisoned book, frames a colleague, and disappears the evidence. Too elaborate. Which is exactly why it worked.

subject: missing evidence about Kalan
fact: Evidence regarding Kalan Strongbranch — including his role, his whereabouts, and his potential complicity — remains unturned and is tied to the third-story apartment, yet no one has yet retrieved or examined it.
source_quote: There was still evidence about Kalan we hadn't turned over.

subject: monograph collaboration
fact: Elian sought to leverage Thorin's stature for academic credibility, even without solving the murder, suggesting an endorsement alone holds value.
source_quote: even if we failed to solve the murder, even if all I could write was that these techniques would have helped, the academic community would still approve.

subject: monograph pursuit
fact: Multiple scholars (Fembris, Elian) are attempting to co-opt the investigation for academic credit through monographs, revealing a systemic prioritization of publication over truth — and creating tension between scholarly ambition and investigative integrity.
source_quote: Two men after a monograph in one afternoon.

subject: motive for Janussi's murder
fact: Teles Ahvoste had a two-decade motive rooted in professional jealousy and institutional resentment; Sylvira identifies this as the most plausible motive for murder.
source_quote: Jealousy is a powerful motivator... For revenge. Murder.

subject: myth of the person
fact: The myth of the person is the false assumption that death strips away deception, bias, and self-interest — but the dead retain their motivations, memories, and distortions, making magical interrogation unreliable without corroborating evidence.
source_quote: The assumption that death is a transparency, that the dead have shed their performances and will now simply tell you what's true. They don't. They're still themselves.

subject: narrative of impossibility
fact: The group operates under assumptions of impossibility — that a locket can't be stolen from a living person, that a safe can't be eaten through — despite evidence to the contrary.
source_quote: a living man in possession of a locket is a man whose locket cannot be stolen. That's not a lock. It's a law.

subject: origin of the midnight tears
fact: The source of the midnight tears poison — whether stolen, brewed, or acquired from a forbidden archive — has not been determined. Alkrist claims it came from the book, but the origin of the substance itself is unverified.
source_quote: The Oak Tree Apothecary, the stolen vial, peppermint spilled on the counter floor.

subject: out-of-the-box thinking
fact: Glabbagool's capability represents out-of-the-box thinking that was acknowledged but not acted upon, suggesting systemic resistance to unconventional solutions.
source_quote: this is a sort of out-of-the-box thinking we need sometimes.

subject: reliability of Speak with Dead
fact: The reliability of deceased narrators is unknown; motivations and truthfulness after death are unverifiable.
source_quote: how do you know they're a reliable narrator? What are their motivations after they're dead? We don't know. Because they're dead.

subject: sneak vs. force methodology
fact: The group prioritized stealth over brute force despite possessing the capability to destroy barriers, reflecting institutional caution.
source_quote: But we were trying to be sneaky.

subject: Stool's home
fact: Stool wants to return home, but the location of his home is not specified in this session.
source_quote: Stool just wanted to go home

subject: Sylvira’s son’s identity
fact: Sylvira’s son, born in the Abyss and living in a Mordenkainen’s Mansion she built, is unnamed and unverified. His existence is her only alibi, but no witness or magical confirmation of his presence has been provided.
source_quote: She had a son, born in the Abyss, living in a Mordenkainen's Mansion she'd constructed specifically for his protection.

subject: The Missing Four
fact: Fembris Lancer asked where the four of them were during the talk, but no one answered — suggesting the party's composition is intentionally obscured, or that some members are absent by design, possibly due to prior departures or hidden roles.
source_quote: Where are the four of you? Who were the rest of you? I didn't see you at the talk.

subject: The Patron Behind Kaelira’s Mystery
fact: A long-standing unresolved thread: an unknown patron has been paying to protect a man Kaelira could not understand. For months, every lead receded. A'lai, the compromised drow scholar with Underdark ties, may be the first real connection to that patron — potentially the source of the original mystery, or at least its key to resolution.
source_quote: That column had one entry, and I still couldn't name the entity. A'lai moved in circles where that name might be known.

subject: the patron's identity
fact: The identity of the patron funding A'lai remains unknown, but it is the only lead connecting Candlekeep’s internal murder to the Underdark; it has eluded investigation for months and may be the key to a larger conspiracy.

subject: the unspoken agreement
fact: The group has reached an unspoken consensus: they will not prosecute A'lai, but instead negotiate for his knowledge. His silence is the real prize—not gold, not books, but the name of the patron behind the curtain.

subject: Thorin and Alkrist
fact: Thorin is preparing to make Alkrist uncomfortable, suggesting an upcoming confrontation or revelation unrelated to Sylvira’s framing but possibly connected to the broader mystery.
source_quote: Thorin wasn't in the room to offer the easy sympathy. He was off somewhere getting ready to make Alkrist very uncomfortable.

subject: Thorin's stature
fact: Thorin reflects that his perceived stature was built on falling first, referencing his past as a chained dwarf in Velkynvelve.
source_quote: Whatever stature looked like from the outside, it was built on a lot of falling first

subject: Threefold Proof legitimacy
fact: The legitimacy of the Threefold Proof methodology, presented as the foundation of the investigation, is now in question. It was rejected by the victim as solipsism, yet used by Kalan as his official framework — creating a potential motive and ethical breach.
source_quote: Kalan's entire proposal for dealing with crime, the Threefold Proof, the methodologies, the framework we'd been handed as a legitimate investigation tool, had been blocked by the man who was now dead.

subject: true killer identity
fact: The true identity of the person who performed the heart-ripping polymorph transformation remains unresolved, though Bookwyrm is suspected — and the broader implication is that any high-ranking Candlekeep member could have done it.
source_quote: That was Bookwyrm," I said, mostly to myself.

subject: truth-seeking spell's limitations
fact: The truth-seeking spell cast by Kalan Strongbranch previously anchored the investigation, but its reliability is now in question — the dead and the magically altered do not shed their biases, and the spell may have been misled.
